beats.text: A narrow shop lined floor to ceiling with clocks, in grey street light. The brass bell over the door swings as the door opens and makes no sound at all.

beats.text: Someone has wedged its clapper with a twist of paper.

beats.text: Monsieur Roux? C'est moi. L'Irlandais. For the gears.

beats.text: Nothing answers him. Not one tick.

beats.text: I closed the shop on Saturday night. I went to bed. Now it is Sunday, and I come down to wind them, and they are all...

beats.html: Dec looks properly. The regulators, the carriage clocks, the ship's clock, the cat clocks, the cheap plastic one over the workshop door. Every face says nine exactly.

beats.html: It's Monday the twenty-third of March. Have you eaten anything? Had a drink of water?

beats.text: Grey tongue. Cloves. Slate.

beats.text: Did anyone come to the door last night?

beats.speaker: roux

beats.html: The pendulum hangs at a slant. Dec shines his torch up into the case.

beats.text: Well, hello.

beats.text: Somebody wound you, set you to nine, and then jammed you so you couldn't go. On purpose.

beats.text: Ah, now. That's not right at all.

beats.text: What? What's not right?

beats.text: I didn't! That door has the old lock. My father's lock.

beats.text: Well, it hasn't now. It has a thing out of a blister pack.
beats.html: Well, it hasn't now. It has a thing out of a blister pack.

beats.html: See those lines round the keyway? That's a pick. Somebody picked this badly, dragging a rake in and out like he was raking leaves.

beats.text: A professional leaves you nothing. You'd never know I'd been there.

beats.text: He is explaining a lock to a man who has just lost a day of his life, and he can't stop. It is what his mouth does when he is frightened.
beats.html: He is explaining a lock to a man who has just lost a day of his life, and he can't stop. It is what his mouth does when he is frightened.

beats.text: But here's the thing. There's a thumb-turn on this side, and it's locked from the inside.

beats.text: So whoever picked it from the yard never went out this way. It's a stage set.

beats.text: The front. With a key. Or you let them in.

beats.html: Dec unrolls his canvas roll on his knee: twelve picks and two tension wrenches, each in its own pocket. He calls them the cutlery.

beats.text: If I pick it from this side, the pins will tell me...

beats.text: He has the wrench in the keyway and the hook going in after it, tongue between his teeth.
beats.html: He has the wrench in the keyway and the hook going in after it, tongue between his teeth.

beats.text: Out front, the bell over the door rings, loud and clear. Somebody has unjammed it.
beats.html: Out front, the bell over the door rings, loud and clear. Somebody has unjammed it.

beats.text: Do not move, monsieur. And please do not finish whatever it is you are doing to that door.
beats.html: Do not move, monsieur. And please do not finish whatever it is you are doing to that door.

beats.text: Monsieur Hartley.

beats.html: He says the name the way a doctor says the name of a rash.

beats.text: At eleven minutes past nine a neighbour reports a break-in. At nine thirty-one I find you inside, at the back door, with burglary tools.

beats.text: I'm building one for the Fondation Vaulmont. A medieval clockmaker's cell. I was buying gears! Monsieur Roux, tell him!

beats.text: Thank you.

beats.text: Can I say one thing? The back door's locked from the inside. Somebody picked it from the yard to fake a break-in, but they never left that way.

beats.speaker: pichon
beats.text: His tongue.

beats.html: Minus twenty tonight on the plateau, they say. The Clockless One lends us every hour. Tonight, perhaps, you'll learn the price of one.

beats.text: The trap bangs down. Underneath it, the bright modern snap of a steel padlock. Far below, the oak door, and the abbess's key turning in it from outside.
beats.html: The trap bangs down. Underneath it, the bright modern snap of a steel padlock. Far below, the oak door, and the abbess's key turning in it from outside.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Well. That's my key gone.
beats.html: Well. That's my key gone.

beats.text: The wind rises to a howl. Inès moves a step closer to him, and then another.
beats.html: The wind rises to a howl. Inès moves a step closer to him, and then another.

choices.text: Hold on through the night together

beats.text: Black iron cage, black beams. Snow sifts through the slits and settles without melting.
beats.html: Black iron cage, black beams. Snow sifts through the slits and settles without melting.

beats.text: Dec spent half an hour flat on the boards with his thinnest pick, then two picks tied with a bootlace. The padlock sits on the far side of the trap.
beats.html: Dec spent half an hour flat on the boards with his thinnest pick, then two picks tied with a bootlace. The padlock sits on the far side of the trap.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Give me a keyhole and I'll open anything. They didn't give me a keyhole. They gave me a floor.
beats.html: Give me a keyhole and I'll open anything. They didn't give me a keyhole. They gave me a floor.

beats.text: He kills his phone torch to save the battery. Hers died at five past four.
beats.html: He kills his phone torch to save the battery. Hers died at five past four.

beats.text: Inès mutters something long and vicious in Hungarian.
beats.html: Inès mutters something long and vicious in Hungarian.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Say the one with the horse again.
beats.html: Say the one with the horse again.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: It isn't about a horse. It's about your mother and a horse. I'm sorry. I don't know your mother.
beats.html: It isn't about a horse. It's about your mother and a horse. I'm sorry. I don't know your mother.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: She'd love you. She'd be terrified of you.
beats.html: She'd love you. She'd be terrified of you.

beats.text: Minus twenty, Fabien said. Her fingers won't bend. She feels warm and heavy and sleepy, and some old part of her knows that is the bad sign.
beats.html: Minus twenty, Fabien said. Her fingers won't bend. She feels warm and heavy and sleepy, and some old part of her knows that is the bad sign.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Talk to me. You always talk. Don't let me sleep.
beats.html: Talk to me. You always talk. Don't let me sleep.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Right. Right. I've a story about a door in Salthill.
beats.html: Right. Right. I've a story about a door in Salthill.

beats.text: Mrs Kilbride, a stuck mortice, a cat called Pádraig and a sandwich. He tells it in the dark, with both arms.
beats.html: Mrs Kilbride, a stuck mortice, a cat called Pádraig and a sandwich. He tells it in the dark, with both arms.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: ...and Pádraig had the sandwich the whole time. Your turn. Tell me something true.
beats.html: ...and Pádraig had the sandwich the whole time. Your turn. Tell me something true.

beats.text: She is too cold to decide not to.
beats.html: She is too cold to decide not to.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: My father lost days. Zoltán. He drove a bus in Lyon for thirty years and knew every street.
beats.html: My father lost days. Zoltán. He drove a bus in Lyon for thirty years and knew every street.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: He taught me to swear in Hungarian. And to look at things. Ne csak nézd, lásd. Don't just look. See.
beats.html: He taught me to swear in Hungarian. And to look at things. Ne csak nézd, lásd. Don't just look. See.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: At the end he'd wake up in nineteen ninety and dress for work. Every morning I told him, and every morning he was frightened.
beats.html: At the end he'd wake up in nineteen ninety and dress for work. Every morning I told him, and every morning he was frightened.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: These people do it on purpose. Like taking a coin out of a fountain. And they call it a religion.
beats.html: These people do it on purpose. Like taking a coin out of a fountain. And they call it a religion.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: That's why I came.
beats.html: That's why I came.

beats.text: Dec blows into his hands, twice.
beats.html: Dec blows into his hands, twice.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: I'm sorry. Mine dropped dead in the van, outside a chipper on Shop Street. I was in Dublin, wearing a lanyard, because the shop was a bit small for me.
beats.html: I'm sorry. Mine dropped dead in the van, outside a chipper on Shop Street. I was in Dublin, wearing a lanyard, because the shop was a bit small for me.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: I wasn't there. So I ran his shop into the ground, and then I started locking people in rooms. Because I couldn't get out of one.
beats.html: I wasn't there. So I ran his shop into the ground, and then I started locking people in rooms. Because I couldn't get out of one.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: You're not that. I watched you open that lock without the word. You're the most stubborn person I've ever met, and I've met my mother.
beats.html: You're not that. I watched you open that lock without the word. You're the most stubborn person I've ever met, and I've met my mother.

beats.text: He leans against her shoulder, and the shivering stops.
beats.html: He leans against her shoulder, and the shivering stops.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: We'll not mention any of this. After.
beats.html: We'll not mention any of this. After.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Never.
beats.html: Never.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Grand.
beats.html: Grand.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Dec. The torch. Point it up.
beats.html: Dec. The torch. Point it up.

beats.text: Through a square hole in the ceiling the beam finds the bell, huge and green-black, the iron hammer poised beside it. Letters run round its lip.
beats.html: Through a square hole in the ceiling the beam finds the bell, huge and green-black, the iron hammer poised beside it. Letters run round its lip.

beats.text: Inès laughs, short and cracked.
beats.html: Inès laughs, short and cracked.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: The hour is struck by whoever winds. Trahere, to draw up the weight. Whoever holds the clock holds the time.
beats.html: The hour is struck by whoever winds. Trahere, to draw up the weight. Whoever holds the clock holds the time.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Dec. Can you make this go?
beats.html: Dec. Can you make this go?

beats.text: The great stone weight hangs on its chain into the dark. Beside the frame, a square iron shaft, and on the floor a crank some clock-keeper left four hundred years ago.
beats.html: The great stone weight hangs on its chain into the dark. Beside the frame, a square iron shaft, and on the floor a crank some clock-keeper left four hundred years ago.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Ah, now. Ah, now.
beats.html: Ah, now. Ah, now.

beats.text: Every turn takes everything they have. After fifty she isn't cold. After a hundred she's sweating. In the cage a ratchet goes clack, clack, like a huge slow heart.
beats.html: Every turn takes everything they have. After fifty she isn't cold. After a hundred she's sweating. In the cage a ratchet goes clack, clack, like a huge slow heart.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: This is the striking weight. When it's up, I pull this lever and she strikes. Hold the lever and she keeps striking.
beats.html: This is the striking weight. When it's up, I pull this lever and she strikes. Hold the lever and she keeps striking.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Then don't let go.
beats.html: Then don't let go.

beats.text: He reaches into the cage up to the shoulder. She nods. He pulls.
beats.html: He reaches into the cage up to the shoulder. She nods. He pulls.

beats.text: BONG.
beats.html: BONG.

beats.text: The note hits them in the teeth and the ribs, and snow drops off the beams in a cloud. Inès claps her hands over her ears and laughs.
beats.html: The note hits them in the teeth and the ribs, and snow drops off the beams in a cloud. Inès claps her hands over her ears and laughs.

beats.text: Seven. Eight. Nine. Out through the slits, down the valley, over the sleeping farms.
beats.html: Seven. Eight. Nine. Out through the slits, down the valley, over the sleeping farms.

beats.text: Ten. Eleven. Twelve.
beats.html: Ten. Eleven. Twelve.

beats.text: Thirteen.
beats.html: Thirteen.

beats.text: Dec lets go. The silence rings.
beats.html: Dec lets go. The silence rings.

beats.text: Her hand touches paper, wedged under the bottom bar of the frame. The winding has shaken it out an inch. It is a leaf of parchment with a charred edge, a page the sisters never managed to burn.
beats.html: Her hand touches paper, wedged under the bottom bar of the frame. The winding has shaken it out an inch. It is a leaf of parchment with a charred edge, a page the sisters never managed to burn.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: I. Custos Horae Ultimae. The Keeper of the Last Hour.
beats.html: I. Custos Horae Ultimae. The Keeper of the Last Hour.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: The Collector.
beats.html: The Collector.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: The Seventh will collect.
beats.html: The Seventh will collect.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: They aren't people. They're offices, like a government. Somebody holds each one. Today.
beats.html: They aren't people. They're offices, like a government. Somebody holds each one. Today.

beats.text: Far down the valley a high, angry engine is coming. And sirens.
beats.html: Far down the valley a high, angry engine is coming. And sirens.

beats.text: Bolt-cutters bite through the padlock. Up comes the volunteer fire brigade of Les Bréviaires in yellow helmets, all talking at once. The bell hasn't rung since sixteen ten.
beats.html: Bolt-cutters bite through the padlock. Up comes the volunteer fire brigade of Les Bréviaires in yellow helmets, all talking at once. The bell hasn't rung since sixteen ten.

beats.speaker: clothilde
beats.text: Well. You've woken the dead. I suppose that's something.
beats.html: Well. You've woken the dead. I suppose that's something.

beats.speaker: clothilde
beats.text: Drink. Don't argue.
beats.html: Drink. Don't argue.

beats.text: Coffee and plum brandy, half and half. It goes down like a lit match.
beats.html: Coffee and plum brandy, half and half. It goes down like a lit match.

beats.text: Dec's phone, warm from his skin, has six per cent. He scrolls back to the very first photograph, enlarges it and holds it out to her.
beats.html: Dec's phone, warm from his skin, has six per cent. He scrolls back to the very first photograph, enlarges it and holds it out to her.

beats.text: Inès knows the hand. Four years of yellow notes on her bench. Inès, client called again, voilà, could you possibly...
beats.html: Inès knows the hand. Four years of yellow notes on her bench. Inès, client called again, voilà, could you possibly...

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Our restorer is close to the word.
beats.html: Our restorer is close to the word.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Not me. Him.
beats.html: Not me. Him.

beats.text: She watches the snow all the way down.
beats.html: She watches the snow all the way down.

beats.text: A white quilt, red geraniums on the sill, a travel clock by the bed and a cuckoo clock by the door. Roux's drawings are spread over the bed.
beats.html: A white quilt, red geraniums on the sill, a travel clock by the bed and a cuckoo clock by the door. Roux's drawings are spread over the bed.

beats.text: Inès is up at the museum with the brown page and a Latin dictionary the size of a breeze block. At breakfast they talked about the weather for twenty minutes, very carefully.
beats.html: Inès is up at the museum with the brown page and a Latin dictionary the size of a breeze block. At breakfast they talked about the weather for twenty minutes, very carefully.

beats.text: A knock. The corridor is empty. On the floor sits a tray: a white teapot, a cup, two biscuits and a card.
beats.html: A knock. The corridor is empty. On the floor sits a tray: a white teapot, a cup, two biscuits and a card.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Ah, Madame Jobin. You're a dote.
beats.html: Ah, Madame Jobin. You're a dote.

beats.text: The tea is hot and spiced. He drinks half the cup in one go.
beats.html: The tea is hot and spiced. He drinks half the cup in one go.

beats.text: Then he stops with the cup halfway to the saucer.
beats.html: Then he stops with the cup halfway to the saucer.

beats.text: Something faint lies under the spice, sweet and dusty. Behind it sits something flat and mineral, like cold wet stone, at the back of his tongue. His tongue feels a size too big.
beats.html: Something faint lies under the spice, sweet and dusty. Behind it sits something flat and mineral, like cold wet stone, at the back of his tongue. His tongue feels a size too big.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Madame Jobin never leaves a tray. She stays and asks about the honeymoon. Nobody stayed.
beats.html: Madame Jobin never leaves a tray. She stays and asks about the honeymoon. Nobody stayed.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Ah, stop. It's the house blend. The cold's got into your head.
beats.html: Ah, stop. It's the house blend. The cold's got into your head.

beats.text: The pot is still nearly full, and he is still cold to the bone.
beats.html: The pot is still nearly full, and he is still cold to the bone.

choices.text: Cloves and slate, like Roux: spit it out and play dead
It's only the house's spiced tea: finish the cup

beats.text: The white quilt, Roux's drawings, the tray. The cup is half empty.
beats.html: The white quilt, Roux's drawings, the tray. The cup is half empty.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Cloves. Cloves and slate.
beats.html: Cloves. Cloves and slate.

beats.text: Roux, in his head, a bit deaf and very angry: everything tastes of cloves. Dec sets the cup down with great care. Then he crosses the room in two strides, sticks two fingers down his throat and is sick into Madame Jobin's geraniums, thoroughly. He will later call it professional.
beats.html: Roux, in his head, a bit deaf and very angry: everything tastes of cloves. Dec sets the cup down with great care. Then he crosses the room in two strides, sticks two fingers down his throat and is sick into Madame Jobin's geraniums, thoroughly. He will later call it professional.

beats.text: He kneels by the window, eyes streaming. His head feels light, like after the second pint. The tea or the fear, he can't tell.
beats.html: He kneels by the window, eyes streaming. His head feels light, like after the second pint. The tea or the fear, he can't tell.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Whoever left that tray is coming back. To see if it worked. To do the clocks.
beats.html: Whoever left that tray is coming back. To see if it worked. To do the clocks.

beats.text: He looks at the pot, still nearly full. Five seconds.
beats.html: He looks at the pot, still nearly full. Five seconds.

beats.text: He pours it down the sink, all but a finger's depth. He half fills the cup with water and leaves it where a man would who drank half and fell asleep. He eats both biscuits, because that man would have.
beats.html: He pours it down the sink, all but a finger's depth. He half fills the cup with water and leaves it where a man would who drank half and fell asleep. He eats both biscuits, because that man would have.

beats.text: Then he lies down on the quilt, facing the door, one arm hanging off the bed, eyes almost shut.
beats.html: Then he lies down on the quilt, facing the door, one arm hanging off the bed, eyes almost shut.

beats.text: Twice the room tilts, gently, like a boat, and tilts back. He bites the inside of his cheek.
beats.html: Twice the room tilts, gently, like a boat, and tilts back. He bites the inside of his cheek.

beats.text: The key turns in the lock.
beats.html: The key turns in the lock.

beats.text: Calm and attentive, almost kind, like a nurse on his rounds. He looks into the cup, then the pot, and nods to himself.
beats.html: Calm and attentive, almost kind, like a nurse on his rounds. He looks into the cup, then the pot, and nods to himself.

beats.text: Then he goes to work, quick and silent, like a man laying a table he has laid a hundred times. Dec's watch, set to 09:00. The travel clock, stopped at nine, a sliver of brass pushed into the movement. The cuckoo clock by the door, set to nine from a chair, its pendulum wedged.
beats.html: Then he goes to work, quick and silent, like a man laying a table he has laid a hundred times. Dec's watch, set to 09:00. The travel clock, stopped at nine, a sliver of brass pushed into the movement. The cuckoo clock by the door, set to nine from a chair, its pendulum wedged.

beats.text: Then he picks up Dec's phone.
beats.html: Then he picks up Dec's phone.

beats.text: Dec's heart stops, and starts again twice as fast.
beats.html: Dec's heart stops, and starts again twice as fast.

beats.text: The phone is locked. Fabien takes Dec's hand gently, the way you'd take a child's, and presses his thumb to the button. It opens.
beats.html: The phone is locked. Fabien takes Dec's hand gently, the way you'd take a child's, and presses his thumb to the button. It opens.

beats.text: He scrolls the photographs without a flicker, deletes them, empties the deleted folder, and sets the phone's clock to nine.
beats.html: He scrolls the photographs without a flicker, deletes them, empties the deleted folder, and sets the phone's clock to nine.

beats.text: Last, he opens the wardrobe, takes out a stick of chalk and draws on the bare pine inside the door with his head on one side.
beats.html: Last, he opens the wardrobe, takes out a stick of chalk and draws on the bare pine inside the door with his head on one side.

beats.text: At the door he looks back at Dec, and his lips move. Latin, very quiet. A prayer, perhaps. For Dec, or for himself.
beats.html: At the door he looks back at Dec, and his lips move. Latin, very quiet. A prayer, perhaps. For Dec, or for himself.

beats.text: The key turns. Dec lies staring at the chalk, so angry he can no longer feel his hands.
beats.html: The key turns. Dec lies staring at the chalk, so angry he can no longer feel his hands.

scenes.label: ch_08_s03
scenes.title: The village street of Les Bréviaires

beats.text: Dec counts sixty, climbs out over the geraniums and slides off the porch roof into a snowdrift. It is not a rooftop chase. He will be firm about that afterwards.
beats.html: Dec counts sixty, climbs out over the geraniums and slides off the porch roof into a snowdrift. It is not a rooftop chase. He will be firm about that afterwards.

beats.text: Fabien walks up the street openly, past the lit windows of the workshops, to a small dark house at the edge of the forest. Smoke from the chimney. A big black four-by-four outside.
beats.html: Fabien walks up the street openly, past the lit windows of the workshops, to a small dark house at the edge of the forest. Smoke from the chimney. A big black four-by-four outside.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: The bald man. He didn't take the train. He drove.
beats.html: The bald man. He didn't take the train. He drove.

beats.text: Fabien stops by the woodpile and makes a call, low and respectful, a junior clerk to a senior partner. Dec crouches behind a stack of logs ten metres away.
beats.html: Fabien stops by the woodpile and makes a call, low and respectful, a junior clerk to a senior partner. Dec crouches behind a stack of logs ten metres away.

beats.speaker: fabien
beats.text: Yes, the Irishman. Half the pot at least. He'll sleep until tomorrow night. The photographs are gone. I saw to it.
beats.html: Yes, the Irishman. Half the pot at least. He'll sleep until tomorrow night. The photographs are gone. I saw to it.

beats.speaker: fabien
beats.text: The woman is at the museum with the old nun. She'll find him in the morning. She'll find the chalk.
beats.html: The woman is at the museum with the old nun. She'll find him in the morning. She'll find the chalk.

beats.speaker: fabien
beats.text: And Morel? He'll have the word by Sunday? Good. And then... yes. Of course. As the rule says.
beats.html: And Morel? He'll have the word by Sunday? Good. And then... yes. Of course. As the rule says.

beats.text: Behind the logs, Dec goes cold all over again.
beats.html: Behind the logs, Dec goes cold all over again.

beats.speaker: fabien
beats.text: The guests. The minister. The prefect, yes, he's confirmed. Two bankers from the Bourse, the journalist from the television, the cardinal's secretary.
beats.html: The guests. The minister. The prefect, yes, he's confirmed. Two bankers from the Bourse, the journalist from the television, the cardinal's secretary.

beats.speaker: fabien
beats.text: The catering is ours. The wine at half past two, half an hour before None. They'll wake remembering the eclipse, the clocks stopping and your voice. Only that. And they'll tell it on camera, all the same way. A miracle.
beats.html: The catering is ours. The wine at half past two, half an hour before None. They'll wake remembering the eclipse, the clocks stopping and your voice. Only that. And they'll tell it on camera, all the same way. A miracle.

beats.text: For the first time, there is warmth in his voice.
beats.html: For the first time, there is warmth in his voice.

beats.speaker: fabien
beats.text: And the Seventh will collect. Nine minutes of every signal in Paris, the markets in a panic. The fund's positions are... Forgive me. Not my concern.
beats.html: And the Seventh will collect. Nine minutes of every signal in Paris, the markets in a panic. The fund's positions are... Forgive me. Not my concern.

beats.speaker: fabien
beats.text: The train worked beautifully. I got off at Saignelégier and our brother drove me up. They walked straight in. Mutuo datum, Brother.
beats.html: The train worked beautifully. I got off at Saignelégier and our brother drove me up. They walked straight in. Mutuo datum, Brother.

beats.text: He hangs up. Dec shifts to ease his cramp, and the German geologist's boot slips off a frozen log. The top of the stack rolls into the snow, knock, knock, knock.
beats.html: He hangs up. Dec shifts to ease his cramp, and the German geologist's boot slips off a frozen log. The top of the stack rolls into the snow, knock, knock, knock.

beats.text: Fabien's head comes round.
beats.html: Fabien's head comes round.

beats.text: Five stone steps down, and a smell so thick Dec could lean on it. In the grey light from a grating, rows of tall round cheeses ripen in perfect silence.
beats.html: Five stone steps down, and a smell so thick Dec could lean on it. In the grey light from a grating, rows of tall round cheeses ripen in perfect silence.

beats.text: A torch beam comes down the steps. Over the cheeses. Over the wet flagstones. It stops a metre from his knees, on his footprints. Then it goes away.
beats.html: A torch beam comes down the steps. Over the cheeses. Over the wet flagstones. It stops a metre from his knees, on his footprints. Then it goes away.

beats.speaker: fabien
beats.text: Rien. Cheese.
beats.html: Rien. Cheese.

beats.text: A grunt. A very large, very low grunt.
beats.html: A grunt. A very large, very low grunt.

beats.text: The door shuts. A wooden bar drops across it outside, clunk. The four-by-four coughs into life and its lights sweep away down the valley.
beats.html: The door shuts. A wooden bar drops across it outside, clunk. The four-by-four coughs into life and its lights sweep away down the valley.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Locked in. Again. That's three times this week. That's a personal best.
beats.html: Locked in. Again. That's three times this week. That's a personal best.

beats.text: The cheeses don't reply. A bar on the outside. On the inside, no handle, no keyhole.
beats.html: The cheeses don't reply. A bar on the outside. On the inside, no handle, no keyhole.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: At least it's not minus twenty. It's about minus two, though. I'm going to die in a cheese cave, and they'll put that on my headstone in Galway.
beats.html: At least it's not minus twenty. It's about minus two, though. I'm going to die in a cheese cave, and they'll put that on my headstone in Galway.

beats.text: An engine, old and clattering, a fan belt screaming on the corners. Boots crunch. The bar lifts, the door opens, and Dec falls backwards into the snow.
beats.html: An engine, old and clattering, a fan belt screaming on the corners. Boots crunch. The bar lifts, the door opens, and Dec falls backwards into the snow.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: How did you...
beats.html: How did you...

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: I went to your room to tell you about the page. Chalk in your wardrobe. Sick in Madame Jobin's geraniums. Your window open.
beats.html: I went to your room to tell you about the page. Chalk in your wardrobe. Sick in Madame Jobin's geraniums. Your window open.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Footprints from the window, up the street, to the logs, into here. Your feet are very easy to follow. They're very big.
beats.html: Footprints from the window, up the street, to the logs, into here. Your feet are very easy to follow. They're very big.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: They know we know, Inès. And they've wiped my phone.
beats.html: They know we know, Inès. And they've wiped my phone.

beats.speaker: clothilde
beats.text: Get in the van. Arguing in the snow is for Protestants.
beats.html: Get in the van. Arguing in the snow is for Protestants.

beats.text: Cheese crates and diesel. Clothilde takes the hairpins far too fast for the night train to Basel.
beats.html: Cheese crates and diesel. Clothilde takes the hairpins far too fast for the night train to Basel.

beats.text: He tells her everything, down to the wine at half past two, and Morel, and as the rule says.
beats.html: He tells her everything, down to the wine at half past two, and Morel, and as the rule says.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Your phone's wiped. Mine isn't.
beats.html: Your phone's wiped. Mine isn't.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Mine had four per cent in the tower. Before it died I took the ledger, the REMIT page and the list of tests. Vincennes, the quai de la Rapée, Austerlitz.
beats.html: Mine had four per cent in the tower. Before it died I took the ledger, the REMIT page and the list of tests. Vincennes, the quai de la Rapée, Austerlitz.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Not the flyleaf. Not the Panthéon page. Those were on yours. It's not enough.
beats.html: Not the flyleaf. Not the Panthéon page. Those were on yours. It's not enough.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Clothilde did it with a prayer. Don't make a thing of it.
beats.html: Clothilde did it with a prayer. Don't make a thing of it.

beats.text: His phone buzzes against the cushion.
beats.html: His phone buzzes against the cushion.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: He wants me inside. Grand. Galerie du dôme, the notebook said. That's the walk round the outside, on every tourist map.
beats.html: He wants me inside. Grand. Galerie du dôme, the notebook said. That's the walk round the outside, on every tourist map.

beats.text: Fabien wiped the photograph. But Inès read that line over Dec's shoulder in the tower, by his torch, and said it out loud. She has said it to herself every night since.
beats.html: Fabien wiped the photograph. But Inès read that line over Dec's shoulder in the tower, by his torch, and said it out loud. She has said it to herself every night since.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Wait.
beats.html: Wait.

beats.text: She opens the list of tests on her phone, all she kept of Morel's notebook.
beats.html: She opens the list of tests on her phone, all she kept of Morel's notebook.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Every test reaches further. Jean-Paul checked the range. On long wave, range means a long wire, hung high.
beats.html: Every test reaches further. Jean-Paul checked the range. On long wave, range means a long wire, hung high.

beats.text: In Morel's drawer of gift-shop rubbish she finds a postcard of the Panthéon.
beats.html: In Morel's drawer of gift-shop rubbish she finds a postcard of the Panthéon.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Sixty-seven metres of steel, hanging free in the middle of Paris. It isn't only a pendulum, Dec. It's an aerial.
beats.html: Sixty-seven metres of steel, hanging free in the middle of Paris. It isn't only a pendulum, Dec. It's an aerial.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Not the gallery outside. The one inside, at the top, where the cable hangs from.
beats.html: Not the gallery outside. The one inside, at the top, where the cable hangs from.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Then I swap the wine at half past two, the way Fabien said on the phone. And then I go up with the word.
beats.html: Then I swap the wine at half past two, the way Fabien said on the phone. And then I go up with the word.

beats.text: The cell in the crypt is finished, and with the pass nobody stops him.
beats.html: The cell in the crypt is finished, and with the pass nobody stops him.

beats.text: Kessler fills the arch of the roped south stair. The narrow north stair inside the wall has a new chain and a shiny brass padlock.
beats.html: Kessler fills the arch of the roped south stair. The narrow north stair inside the wall has a new chain and a shiny brass padlock.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Two minutes, that. Later, when nobody's looking.
beats.html: Two minutes, that. Later, when nobody's looking.

beats.text: The CECI N'EST PAS UNE BOMBE crate goes over with theatrical surprise. Four hundred gears ring across the stone like all the coins in the world.
beats.html: The CECI N'EST PAS UNE BOMBE crate goes over with theatrical surprise. Four hundred gears ring across the stone like all the coins in the world.

beats.text: Behind the screen, four pewter jugs of the real wine go into the empty crate. Four jugs of vin chaud with a spoon of cocoa take their place.
beats.html: Behind the screen, four pewter jugs of the real wine go into the empty crate. Four jugs of vin chaud with a spoon of cocoa take their place.

beats.speaker: moussa
beats.text: Eleven euros forty an hour. For this, I want twelve.
beats.html: Eleven euros forty an hour. For this, I want twelve.

beats.text: At half past two the trays go out. The minister drinks. The prefect drinks. The cardinal's secretary asks for a second cup.
beats.html: At half past two the trays go out. The minister drinks. The prefect drinks. The cardinal's secretary asks for a second cup.

beats.text: Dec watches them drink harmless wine and breathes out. Then he walks to the north aisle, not hurrying.
beats.html: Dec watches them drink harmless wine and breathes out. Then he walks to the north aisle, not hurrying.

beats.text: Vaulmont's voice fills the nave behind him. Everyone is facing the stage.
beats.html: Vaulmont's voice fills the nave behind him. Everyone is facing the stage.

beats.speaker: vaulmont
beats.text: ...and when the light is taken from us, my friends, we will see what we truly owe...
beats.html: ...and when the light is taken from us, my friends, we will see what we truly owe...

beats.text: Seventy seconds. The shackle drops, and he goes up into the dark two steps at a time, the word ready in his mouth.
beats.html: Seventy seconds. The shackle drops, and he goes up into the dark two steps at a time, the word ready in his mouth.

beats.text: By the easel, Inès feels a hum in her back teeth. It comes down the steel cable from the dome, and the brass sphere carries it past her.
beats.html: By the easel, Inès feels a hum in her back teeth. It comes down the steel cable from the dome, and the brass sphere carries it past her.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Go on, Dec. Go on.
beats.html: Go on, Dec. Go on.

beats.text: Forty steps up, a torch hits him from below.
beats.html: Forty steps up, a torch hits him from below.

beats.text: Not police. The prefect's own protection detail, who answer to the man in the front row and not to any commissaire. They have just watched a contractor pick a lock twenty metres from a minister.
beats.html: Not police. The prefect's own protection detail, who answer to the man in the front row and not to any commissaire. They have just watched a contractor pick a lock twenty metres from a minister.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: There's a radio up there! On the cable! Two minutes, I only need two minutes!
beats.html: There's a radio up there! On the cable! Two minutes, I only need two minutes!

beats.text: They don't need two minutes. They need four seconds, and one of them twists his wrist until the picks fall.
beats.html: They don't need two minutes. They need four seconds, and one of them twists his wrist until the picks fall.

beats.text: They are marching him down the north aisle when the light goes. The dome turns deep blue, and outside thousands of people sigh at once.
beats.html: They are marching him down the north aisle when the light goes. The dome turns deep blue, and outside thousands of people sigh at once.

beats.text: Phones light up all over the nave, every screen at 09:00. Through the great doors the traffic lights of the rue Soufflot flash red.
beats.html: Phones light up all over the nave, every screen at 09:00. Through the great doors the traffic lights of the rue Soufflot flash red.

beats.text: And the guests see it, wide awake and sober, cups in their hands. They will remember every second, because Dec made sure of it.
beats.html: And the guests see it, wide awake and sober, cups in their hands. They will remember every second, because Dec made sure of it.

beats.text: The minister stands up. The cardinal's secretary crosses himself.
beats.html: The minister stands up. The cardinal's secretary crosses himself.

beats.speaker: vaulmont
beats.text: Do not be afraid. For nine minutes the city will hear its debt. Mutuo datum.
beats.html: Do not be afraid. For nine minutes the city will hear its debt. Mutuo datum.

beats.speaker: vaulmont
beats.text: Reddetur.
beats.html: Reddetur.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: It's a radio! It's a box in the dome! It's a radio!
beats.html: It's a radio! It's a box in the dome! It's a radio!

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Inès! Tell them!
beats.html: Inès! Tell them!

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Nobody's listening.
beats.html: Nobody's listening.

beats.text: At three the light comes back, silver and slow. Vaulmont lifts one hand, and the station clock lurches round to three.
beats.html: At three the light comes back, silver and slow. Vaulmont lifts one hand, and the station clock lurches round to three.

beats.speaker: vaulmont
beats.text: And now, my friends, it is given back.
beats.html: And now, my friends, it is given back.

beats.text: The nave stands and applauds. Some of them are weeping. The camera's red light stays on.
beats.html: The nave stands and applauds. Some of them are weeping. The camera's red light stays on.

beats.text: Two hundred clocks are ticking, every one of them right.
beats.html: Two hundred clocks are ticking, every one of them right.

beats.speaker: roux
beats.text: LE MIRACLE DU PANTHÉON. Front page. With a photograph of a clock.
beats.html: LE MIRACLE DU PANTHÉON. Front page. With a photograph of a clock.

beats.speaker: roux
beats.text: The Bourse lost billions in nine minutes. And somebody, it says here, has made billions.
beats.html: The Bourse lost billions in nine minutes. And somebody, it says here, has made billions.

beats.speaker: roux
beats.text: Nom de Dieu de nom de Dieu. It's a radio. I told him I wouldn't build it.
beats.html: Nom de Dieu de nom de Dieu. It's a radio. I told him I wouldn't build it.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Somebody else did.
beats.html: Somebody else did.

beats.speaker: roux
beats.text: Where's the Irishman?
beats.html: Where's the Irishman?

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: The prefecture let him go at six this morning. Monsieur de Vaulmont declined to press charges.
beats.html: The prefecture let him go at six this morning. Monsieur de Vaulmont declined to press charges.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: A foreigner, overexcited by an eclipse. He told them he'd hate to spoil such a beautiful day.
beats.html: A foreigner, overexcited by an eclipse. He told them he'd hate to spoil such a beautiful day.

beats.text: The easel is empty. Dec sits on the sofa, a bruise coming up on one wrist.
beats.html: The easel is empty. Dec sits on the sofa, a bruise coming up on one wrist.

beats.text: A courier has left two envelopes: one cream, one with a bank's blue logo.
beats.html: A courier has left two envelopes: one cream, one with a bank's blue logo.

beats.text: Clipped to it is a cheque: the fee for the Clockmaker's Cell, exactly as Dec invoiced it, to the cent.
beats.html: Clipped to it is a cheque: the fee for the Clockmaker's Cell, exactly as Dec invoiced it, to the cent.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: He paid me. And he let me go.
beats.html: He paid me. And he let me go.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Of course he did. He keeps accounts.
beats.html: Of course he did. He keeps accounts.

beats.text: She opens the blue envelope.
beats.html: She opens the blue envelope.

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: He's called in the atelier. My bench, my lamps, Jean-Paul's sofa. Nine days.
beats.html: He's called in the atelier. My bench, my lamps, Jean-Paul's sofa. Nine days.

beats.speaker: dec
beats.text: Your painting?
beats.html: Your painting?

beats.speaker: ines
beats.text: Lent to the Panthéon, it says in the paper. By popular demand.
beats.html: Lent to the Panthéon, it says in the paper. By popular demand.

beats.text: On her bench, under the lamp, her notebook still lies open at one word in pencil. REMITTERE.
beats.html: On her bench, under the lamp, her notebook still lies open at one word in pencil. REMITTERE.

beats.text: She closes it.
beats.html: She closes it.
