beats.ch01.s01.b001: A narrow shop lined floor to ceiling with clocks, in grey street light. The brass bell over the door swings as the door opens and makes no sound at all.
beats.ch01.s01.b002: Someone has wedged its clapper with a twist of paper.
beats.ch01.s01.b004: Monsieur Roux? C'est moi. L'Irlandais. For the gears.
beats.ch01.s01.b005: Nothing answers him. Not one tick.
beats.ch01.s01.b006: Two hundred clocks cover the walls, and all of them are silent. A row of cat clocks has its eyes fixed, every one looking left.
beats.ch01.s01.b007: That's very quiet for a clock shop.
beats.ch01.s01.b010: It's Monday. I said Monday, didn't I? For the escapement wheels.
beats.ch01.s01.b012: Dec. Declan Hartley. I was here Thursday. You called me a thief because I offered you forty euro for a mainspring.
beats.ch01.s01.b014: Roux says it with relief, as if he has found one thing in the room where he left it.
beats.ch01.s01.b015: I closed the shop on Saturday night. I went to bed. Now it is Sunday, and I come down to wind them, and they are all...
beats.ch01.s01.b016: He lifts one hand and lets it fall.
beats.ch01.s01.b018: Dec looks properly. The regulators, the carriage clocks, the ship's clock, the cat clocks, the cheap plastic one over the workshop door. Every face says nine exactly.
beats.ch01.s01.b020: Right. Okay. That's a lot of nine.
beats.ch01.s01.b022: This time it is a question from a very old man, and his voice cracks on it.
beats.ch01.s01.b023: Dec comes round the counter. Roux smells of machine oil and pipe tobacco, and of something sweet and dusty.
beats.ch01.s01.b024: It's Monday the twenty-third of March. Have you eaten anything? Had a drink of water?
beats.ch01.s01.b025: I had my coffee. Everything tastes of cloves. Cloves and slate. Like licking a church roof.
beats.ch01.s01.b026: He sticks his tongue out like a child at bad medicine. It is the wrong colour: a dull smeared grey, as if he has been sucking a pencil.
beats.ch01.s01.b029: Dec files it away, the way his father taught him to keep the screws from a lock: in the order they came out.
beats.ch01.s01.b030: Somebody has been in here. They have been touching my clocks.
beats.ch01.s01.b031: Did anyone come to the door last night?
beats.ch01.s01.b032: Nobody comes to the door. I lock the front, I lock the back, I go upstairs, I sleep, I come down. And now it is Sunday.
beats.ch01.s02.b001: A tall plain oak clock stands by the counter, the kind a farmer hangs his hat on. Behind its little glass window, the pendulum hangs dead.
beats.ch01.s02.b003: The pendulum hangs at a slant. Dec shines his torch up into the case.
beats.ch01.s02.b005: A sliver of brass, no bigger than a matchstick, has been pushed between the crutch and the pendulum rod.
beats.ch01.s02.b007: Somebody wound you, set you to nine, and then jammed you so you couldn't go. On purpose.
beats.ch01.s02.b008: Lower down, on the bare oak inside the trunk, there is chalk.
beats.ch01.s02.b010: It is small and careful. Whoever drew it had all the time in the world.
beats.ch01.s02.b011: Monsieur Roux? Did you draw something in your clock?
beats.ch01.s02.b014: He takes a photograph without touching the chalk, and closes the little door the way you close a door on a sleeping baby. Or a bomb.
beats.ch01.s03.b001: Trays of springs and wheels lie like jewels under a strip light. At the far end is the back door to the courtyard.
beats.ch01.s03.b003: The door is locked. Dec looks at it with a professional's interest, and then with a different kind.
beats.ch01.s03.b004: Ah, now. That's not right at all.
beats.ch01.s03.b006: When did you put a new lock on your back door?
beats.ch01.s03.b007: I didn't! That door has the old lock. My father's lock.
beats.ch01.s03.b008: Well, it hasn't now. It has a thing out of a blister pack.
beats.ch01.s03.b010: See those lines round the keyway? That's a pick. Somebody picked this badly, dragging a rake in and out like he was raking leaves.
beats.ch01.s03.b011: A professional leaves you nothing. You'd never know I'd been there.
beats.ch01.s03.b012: He is explaining a lock to a man who has just lost a day of his life, and he can't stop. It is what his mouth does when he is frightened.
beats.ch01.s03.b013: But here's the thing. There's a thumb-turn on this side, and it's locked from the inside.
beats.ch01.s03.b014: So whoever picked it from the yard never went out this way. It's a stage set.
beats.ch01.s03.b015: Then how did they come in?
beats.ch01.s03.b016: The front. With a key. Or you let them in.
beats.ch01.s03.b017: Dec unrolls his canvas roll on his knee: twelve picks and two tension wrenches, each in its own pocket. He calls them the cutlery.
beats.ch01.s03.b018: If I pick it from this side, the pins will tell me...
beats.ch01.s03.b019: He has the wrench in the keyway and the hook going in after it, tongue between his teeth.
beats.ch01.s03.b020: Out front, the bell over the door rings, loud and clear. Somebody has unjammed it.
beats.ch01.s03.b021: Do not move, monsieur. And please do not finish whatever it is you are doing to that door.
beats.ch01.s04.b001: Two young officers fill the doorway. Between them stands a round, tired man.
beats.ch01.s04.b003: Commissaire Pichon. Police judiciaire. And you are?
beats.ch01.s04.b004: Dec. Declan Hartley. Look, this isn't what it looks like.
beats.ch01.s04.b005: Pichon looks at it: the man on his knees, the hook in the keyhole, eleven more picks laid out like surgical instruments.
beats.ch01.s04.b006: That is the thief! He wanted my mainspring for forty euros!
beats.ch01.s04.b008: He says the name the way a doctor says the name of a rash.
beats.ch01.s04.b009: At eleven minutes past nine a neighbour reports a break-in. At nine thirty-one I find you inside, at the back door, with burglary tools.
beats.ch01.s04.b010: I was at breakfast. I would like to go back to breakfast. Please make it easy for me.
beats.ch01.s04.b011: I'm a locksmith. I build escape rooms. You lock people in a room, they find the clues, they pay you.
beats.ch01.s04.b012: I'm building one for the Fondation Vaulmont. A medieval clockmaker's cell. I was buying gears! Monsieur Roux, tell him!
beats.ch01.s04.b014: He is a thief. But I don't think he stopped my clocks. He can't even get the price of a mainspring right.
beats.ch01.s04.b016: Stand up, please. Slowly. Leave the little knives on the floor.
beats.ch01.s04.b017: They're picks, not knives. They wouldn't cut butter.
beats.ch01.s04.b018: Dec stands and leaves the cutlery on the floor. An officer takes his arm, not roughly, and turns him to face the wall.
beats.ch01.s04.b020: Can I say one thing? The back door's locked from the inside. Somebody picked it from the yard to fake a break-in, but they never left that way.
beats.ch01.s04.b021: And the clocks were stopped on purpose. There's brass jammed in the pendulum, and a drawing in chalk inside his clock. A clock with nine at the top.
beats.ch01.s04.b022: And his tongue's gone grey. He says everything tastes of cloves.
beats.ch01.s04.b023: There is a pause behind him.
beats.ch01.s04.b025: Another pause, longer. When Pichon speaks again, his voice has sat up.
beats.ch01.s04.b026: A clock. With nine at the top.
beats.ch01.s04.b027: In the longcase. Inside the door.
beats.ch01.s04.b028: Footsteps cross the shop. The little door of the longcase opens. There is only the silence of two hundred stopped clocks and a delivery van beeping somewhere in the street.
beats.ch01.s04.b029: The little door closes again, very softly.
beats.ch01.s04.b031: Monsieur Hartley. You are under arrest.
beats.ch01.s04.b032: For what? I've just told you...
beats.ch01.s04.b033: Exactly. You have told me a great deal more than you should know.
beats.ch01.s04.b034: He tucks the folded napkin into his raincoat pocket and nods to the door, where the street and the police car wait.
beats.ch01.s04.b035: Come. We will talk about it over lunch.
beats.ch01.s04.b036: Dec looks back once at the longcase clock, at Roux on his stool, at the cutlery on the floor.
beats.ch01.s04.b037: He has never in his life managed to keep his mouth shut, and this doesn't feel like the morning to start.
beats.ch02.s01.b001: A top-floor workshop under a grey skylight. The radiator knocks like a polite ghost. On the big easel, a dark old painting, a third of its sky cleaned to a cold clear blue.
beats.ch02.s01.b003: An Allegory of the Sundial, French, about 1650. A woman in a garden rests one hand on a stone sundial and points at the sky with the other.
beats.ch02.s01.b004: You had better not have been retouched in the eighteen hundreds. I don't have time for it.
beats.ch02.s01.b005: The odd thing is the sundial. Its shadow falls on a smooth blank band where the hours should run.
beats.ch02.s01.b009: En somme, Lassalle telephoned again. The client asks if we can finish by the end of the month.
beats.ch02.s01.b010: We said the fifteenth of April.
beats.ch02.s01.b011: Voilà, we said. But the client has an event on the first.
beats.ch02.s01.b012: I am not taking a scalpel to a seventeenth-century sky because somebody is having a party. Who is the client?
beats.ch02.s01.b013: Lassalle doesn't say. A private collection.
beats.ch02.s01.b014: His eyes go straight to the sundial, and stay there.
beats.ch02.s01.b015: And there's nothing unusual? Underneath? Old repairs, overpaint?
beats.ch02.s01.b017: No reason. I'll be in the office. If there's anything.
beats.ch02.s01.b018: He shuts himself in his glass office and sits with his hands flat on the desk.
beats.ch02.s01.b019: People don't ask that idly. They ask it about paintings they already know the answer to.
beats.ch02.s02.b001: Under ultraviolet the old varnish shines a milky green. Except in one place.
beats.ch02.s02.b003: On the face of the sundial the glow breaks into a faint dark ring, with twelve small marks round its rim.
beats.ch02.s02.b004: She swaps the lamp for a raking light, almost flat to the canvas, so every ridge in the paint throws a shadow.
beats.ch02.s02.b007: Below the dial runs a line of Roman capitals, also painted out. One word in the middle has been scraped away with a blade, down to the ground.
beats.ch02.s02.b009: Mutuo datum. Given as a loan. And hora nona, the ninth hour.
beats.ch02.s02.b010: She takes forty-one photographs and logs every one. A photograph without a note is a rumour.
beats.ch02.s02.b011: Through the glass, Morel has not come out to ask why the blind is down. He is not looking at her, very hard.
beats.ch02.s02.b012: At nine thirty-five the radio over the sink says rue des Gravilliers.
beats.ch02.s02.b013: An elderly clockmaker found confused in his shop... he had, quote, lost a day... all the clocks had been stopped...
beats.ch02.s02.b015: She looks at the painted clock with nine at the top. Then she pulls off her gloves, grabs her mustard scarf and takes the stairs at a speed her mother would not approve of.
beats.ch02.s03.b001: A police car half on the pavement. A small crowd with shopping trolleys, and a man with an elderly dachshund. The dachshund looks at Inès. She goes round the other side of the trolleys.
beats.ch02.s03.b003: Two officers steer a tall man out of the shop. He ducks a beat late and hits his head on the bell.
beats.ch02.s03.b005: No, I understand, I'd arrest me too, on paper I look desperate...
beats.ch02.s03.b006: He sees Inès and gives her an enormous hopeful smile.
beats.ch02.s03.b007: Madame! Could you telephone to my client? J'ai un rendez-vous à onze heures! Je suis une serrure!
beats.ch02.s03.b008: Je ne peux pas. Je vais être en retard.
beats.ch02.s03.b009: And you are not a lock. You are a serrurier. A serrure is the thing you open.
beats.ch02.s03.b010: Right. Thanks. That's actually very helpful. I'll know for next time.
beats.ch02.s03.b012: As they fold him into the car, something falls from his jacket and rings across the cobbles to the toe of her grey boot.
beats.ch02.s03.b014: Through the rear window the Irishman looks back at her, apologising or asking for help.
beats.ch02.s03.b015: Inès pockets the gear and goes to find out where the police judiciaire has its lunch.
beats.ch02.s04.b001: A bare table, a camera, and a door with a card reader and no keyhole, which Dec takes personally.
beats.ch02.s04.b003: You don't mind. If I don't eat at twelve I become unjust. My wife says so.
beats.ch02.s04.b004: Your landlord says you are polite and sing in the shower. Your bank says less.
beats.ch02.s04.b005: And your back door was faked by someone who wishes the police to find a burglar. And go home.
beats.ch02.s04.b006: He puts down his spoon and slides three photographs across the table.
beats.ch02.s04.b008: October, a retired judge. January, a bookseller. February, a curate at Saint-Médard. Every clock at nine. All said everything tasted of cloves.
beats.ch02.s04.b009: None of this was in the papers. Then a man on his knees in the fourth case tells me about the chalk and the cloves before I ask.
beats.ch02.s04.b010: I just looked at what was there.
beats.ch02.s04.b011: Yes. That is the trouble. Most people don't.
beats.ch02.s04.b012: An officer looks in. A woman downstairs has something of the prisoner's. She says the lobby coffee machine is a crime and should be arrested.
beats.ch02.s05.b002: Commissaire. Inès Varga, restorer, Atelier Morel. This fell out of his pocket.
beats.ch02.s05.b003: She sets the brass gear on the table.
beats.ch02.s05.b004: Oh, thanks. That's the pattern piece. It came with the parts list from my client.
beats.ch02.s05.b007: They say it together, and look at each other with mutual irritation.
beats.ch02.s05.b008: The Fondation Vaulmont. Please match all wheels to this pattern. I thought it was their logo...
beats.ch02.s05.b009: He turns it to the light, sees the IX for the first time, and puts it down.
beats.ch02.s05.b010: I saw this mark this morning. Under the varnish of a painting from about sixteen fifty.
beats.ch02.s05.b011: A clock with nine at the top, painted out. A Latin line about a loan and the ninth hour, with one word scraped away. I have photographs.
beats.ch02.s05.b012: Pichon takes off his reading glasses and presses the bridge of his nose.
beats.ch02.s06.b002: Monsieur Hartley, I have nothing against you but bad luck and a bag of little knives. Madame Varga, I keep the gear. Send me your photographs.
beats.ch02.s06.b003: Then go home, both of you. If I find you in the fifth case, I will be very sad, I will eat a large lunch, and then I will put you in a cell.
beats.ch02.s06.b009: I didn't come for you. I came for the mark.
beats.ch02.s06.b010: We're not, you know. Partners or anything.
beats.ch02.s06.b013: They stand in the drizzle not being partners. A bus goes by.
beats.ch02.s06.b014: His phone rings. A Paris number.
beats.ch02.s06.b015: Monsieur Hartley? Mademoiselle Ferrand, Fondation Vaulmont. We heard about this morning's unpleasantness.
beats.ch02.s06.b016: The clockmaker's cell must be installed by the thirty-first. The vigil is on the first of April, the day of the eclipse. Nothing about it can move.
beats.ch02.s06.b017: Monsieur de Vaulmont sends his regards.
beats.ch02.s06.b019: They knew I'd been arrested. Before I'd told a soul.
beats.ch02.s06.b020: Who sent you the parts list?
beats.ch02.s06.b021: Dec digs a crumpled envelope out of his satchel. The sender's stamp is a notary's.
beats.ch02.s06.b023: Lassalle. That's the broker for my painting.
beats.ch03.s01.b001: A stone stairwell, grey light from the street door. Dec sits on the bottom step with two paper cups of coffee and a folded newspaper, like a large untidy dog told to wait.
beats.ch03.s01.b003: I brought coffee. One black, one with everything in it. You take whichever.
beats.ch03.s01.b004: He holds out the black one. She never said which. He guessed wrong. She takes it, mostly to stop him holding it out.
beats.ch03.s01.b006: You told Pichon. I've a very good memory for addresses. It is what we do in my line of work. You remember where the doors are.
beats.ch03.s01.b007: And there is a bad thing.
beats.ch03.s01.b008: He hands her the newspaper, folded to page four.
beats.ch03.s01.b010: Inès reads it twice. The coffee goes cold in her other hand.
beats.ch03.s01.b011: Lassalle. He telephoned Morel on Saturday to ask if we could be faster.
beats.ch03.s01.b012: The man who sent me the gear and the man who sent you the painting. In the river. Of a heart attack. The day the clocks stopped.
beats.ch03.s01.b013: Four floors up, a door bangs. Morel starts down the stairs and stops on the first landing.
beats.ch03.s01.b014: I am going to the quai d'Orléans.
beats.ch03.s01.b015: Grand. I will come with you.
beats.ch03.s01.b017: No, I know. But I have a good feeling about this door.
beats.ch03.s02.b001: The small door set in the green carriage door stands an inch open. Upstairs, the office door stands open all the way.
beats.ch03.s02.b002: Inside, panelled walls and tall windows over the river. Every book lies open on the carpet, spine up, in rows. Every filing drawer is pulled out to exactly the same length. Every picture stands against the wall with its brown paper backing slit down the middle.
beats.ch03.s02.b004: This is not a burglary. Burglars are stupid. This is someone going through a room square by square.
beats.ch03.s02.b005: And they did not find it. They have gone round in a ring. Bookcase, cabinet, pictures. Every drawer of the desk is out.
beats.ch03.s02.b006: But they have not done the desk itself. Either they were interrupted, or they do not know what this is.
beats.ch03.s02.b007: He steps between the open books to a heavy mahogany bureau with a high back of pigeonholes, all emptied onto the floor.
beats.ch03.s02.b008: Second Empire. A workshop in the Faubourg Saint-Antoine made hundreds of these for notaries, and every one has a secret drawer.
beats.ch03.s02.b009: Because they only knew the one trick. Take out the middle pigeonhole, reach in to the elbow, and at the back on the left there is a peg...
beats.ch03.s02.b010: A click. A panel Inès would have sworn was solid drops forward on a hidden hinge. Behind it, a drawer no deeper than a book.
beats.ch03.s02.b011: Every desk of that make. Every single one.
beats.ch03.s02.b013: In the drawer there are three things.
beats.ch03.s02.b017: The gate of hell. The ninth niche.
beats.ch03.s02.b018: The Barrière d'Enfer was an old toll gate in the city wall. At Denfert-Rochereau. Where the catacombs are.
beats.ch03.s02.b020: Inès takes the watch. It is warm. Her thumb finds the catch on the back of the case.
beats.ch03.s02.b021: The floor of the landing creaks. One plank, under one big careful weight.
beats.ch03.s02.b023: His small pale eyes go to the open drawer, then to the watch in Inès's hand. Without a word, he comes into the room.
beats.ch03.s03.b001: Grey zinc slopes wet with drizzle, chimney pots, a satellite dish, a pot of dead geraniums. The Seine far below on one side, a courtyard of bins on the other.
beats.ch03.s03.b006: Behind them the zinc booms under a great weight. The bald man is not running. He walks, as if he has all day.
beats.ch03.s03.b007: At the end of the ridge, the roof stops. A light well drops between two buildings, a metre and a bit wide. On the far side, a lower roof with a skylight propped open on a stick.
beats.ch03.s03.b008: Dec jumps it, skids, catches the skylight frame, and turns round with both hands out.
beats.ch03.s03.b010: No. I cannot. I am afraid of heights. I clean skies. I do not jump over holes.
beats.ch03.s03.b011: You can. It is a metre. You have walked further for a coffee.
beats.ch03.s03.b012: The zinc booms behind her. She looks round.
beats.ch03.s03.b014: He is not looking at her. A grey pigeon is caught by one foot in the bird netting along the gutter, beating itself against the zinc.
beats.ch03.s03.b015: The huge man reaches out slowly, the way you reach for a sleeping child. He folds its wings. With one thick finger he works the net off its foot, holds it a moment against his coat, and opens his hands.
beats.ch03.s03.b016: The pigeon goes up past Inès's face in a clatter of wings.
beats.ch03.s03.b017: And Inès, without deciding to, jumps.
beats.ch03.s03.b018: Dec catches her by both wrists. They go over sideways against the skylight, the stick falls out, and the skylight bangs shut on Dec's elbow.
beats.ch03.s03.b019: Ah, Jaysus, Mary and the holy saints and all their cousins...
beats.ch03.s03.b020: Across the gap, the bald man studies the drop, then takes out a phone and walks slowly back the way he came.
beats.ch03.s04.b001: A stone and iron bridge over a green-grey Seine, the tip of the island behind them, rain on the parapet.
beats.ch03.s04.b004: I could not. And then I did. Do not make a thing of it.
beats.ch03.s04.b006: It was a metre and twenty.
beats.ch03.s04.b007: I will grant you the twenty.
beats.ch03.s04.b008: Her other hand is still clenched round the silver watch. The chain has printed links into her palm. She presses the catch. The back springs open.
beats.ch03.s04.b011: It is the first time she has used his name. He bends over her hand and, for once, goes quiet.
beats.ch03.s05.b001: The shop is ticking again like light rain. Two hundred clocks back at their business, the cat clocks eyes going left and right. Someone has wiped the chalk out of the longcase.
beats.ch03.s05.b003: A day! A whole day! At eighty-one I have counted how many I have left. And the police send me a boy with a pimple to ask if I have been drinking!
beats.ch03.s05.b005: You are the thief who brought me my water. Sit. Mind the cuckoo, he bites.
beats.ch03.s05.b006: Roux will not touch the watch on the counter. He looks at it the way a man looks at a dog that once bit him.
beats.ch03.s05.b007: Anselme. Before Sunday. Did anyone ask you for something you would not do?
beats.ch03.s05.b008: Everybody. That is what a clockmaker is. A man who says no.
beats.ch03.s05.b009: Two jobs this winter. The gentleman came once. After that, only a young man in a grey coat with a parcel.
beats.ch03.s05.b011: Grey suit, very good. Silver hair brushed back. A voice like warm oil. He had one of those on a chain. A very good watch to have no hands.
beats.ch03.s05.b012: Dec and Inès keep their eyes on Roux. It takes some effort.
beats.ch03.s05.b013: The first job was a lock. A copy of a fourteenth-century letter lock. Nine wheels. Turn each to a letter, and if they spell the word, the bar drops.
beats.ch03.s05.b015: I do not know! The drawings give the gates by number, not letter. The young man brought the last wheel's position in a sealed envelope and stood over me while I cut it.
beats.ch03.s05.b016: He said it was a matter of faith. Faith! In my shop!
beats.ch03.s05.b018: The one I did not do. Station clocks, hospital clocks, the receivers in the traffic lights. They all listen to Allouis, the long-wave transmitter. It sends out the real time and every radio clock in France obeys.
beats.ch03.s05.b019: They wanted the receivers changed to listen to a different voice. For an exhibition. I said a clock listens to Allouis as a priest listens to God, and I put him out of my shop. Ten days ago.
beats.ch03.s05.b020: The cuckoo over the workshop door shoots out and says cuckoo four times. Dec jumps.
beats.ch03.s05.b021: Then on Sunday someone takes a day off you. Because you said no.
beats.ch03.s06.b001: Roux spreads five sheets of old drawings from a cardboard tube, weighed down with a carriage clock, a jar of screws, his loupe, and after a moment's thought, the handless watch.
beats.ch03.s06.b003: Brother Anselm Vey made me. Thirteen forty-nine.
beats.ch03.s06.b004: The plague year. Everybody was dying and this one made locks. The word was never on the drawings. The young man said so. Vey kept it in his book.
beats.ch03.s06.b005: It is the same lock. On the watch. It is a picture of this lock.
beats.ch03.s06.b006: Of course. It is their sign. Every one of them carries the lock, and none of them carries the word. You see, thief? You are not so stupid.
beats.ch03.s06.b007: Take the tube. Every time I open it I taste cloves.
beats.ch03.s06.b009: With enormous dignity, he does. Still grey, fainter, like the shadow of a thumbprint on glass.
beats.ch03.s06.b010: I restored an apothecary's sign once. Sixteen hundreds. One panel was a man in bed, tongue grey, spiced wine, cloves round the jug, a plant with white trumpet flowers.
beats.ch03.s06.b011: The rhyme said: give this to a man and he will owe you a day.
beats.ch03.s06.b012: White trumpets. Datura. My grandmother grew it for the rats.
beats.ch03.s06.b013: The anger goes out of his face. What is left is an old man in a work coat.
beats.ch03.s06.b014: Somebody gave me that? And drew in my longcase? My father's clock.
beats.ch03.s06.b015: Dec's hand is on the old man's shoulder. It feels like a bird's.
beats.ch03.s06.b016: We will find out who. I promise you.
beats.ch03.s06.b017: Thief. You promise like a thief.
beats.ch03.s07.b002: The warm-oil man wants the clocks of Paris to hear a different voice. Roux says no and loses a day. Lassalle is in the river. And they want my room finished for an eclipse at the Panthéon.
beats.ch03.s07.b003: I do not know what any of that means.
beats.ch03.s07.b004: Neither do I. But I know where this is.
beats.ch03.s07.b006: Under the ground. With the bones.
beats.ch03.s07.b007: Six million of them, more or less. The ninth niche will not be in the part with the gift shop.
beats.ch03.s07.b008: She scrolls to a number and looks at it as if a wasp has landed on her hand.
beats.ch03.s07.b009: My mother's hairdresser has a cousin who goes down there at night. Illegally. A philosophy student. They call her La Taupe.
beats.ch03.s07.b011: I have never met her. My mother's hairdresser says she is very good, and also completely insane.
beats.ch03.s07.b012: Her thumb hovers over the call button.
beats.ch04.s01.b001: Orange street light, wet brambles, a black cutting below. Somewhere a dog barks and Inès flinches.
beats.ch04.s01.b003: La Taupe looks Dec up and down.
beats.ch04.s01.b006: For the galleries. One metre forty in spots. You'll crack your skull and moan. The tall ones always moan.
beats.ch04.s01.b007: Your mother's hairdresser says you're afraid of everything.
beats.ch04.s01.b009: Underground there's no heights and no dogs. Only water and the dead. You're fine with the dead?
beats.ch04.s01.b010: I restore paintings from the sixteen hundreds. Everyone in them is dead.
beats.ch04.s01.b011: La Taupe considers this, and seems to find it acceptable.
beats.ch04.s01.b013: She pulls two pairs from the backpack. They smell powerfully of old rubber.
beats.ch04.s01.b014: Headlamps. If you lose me, stand still and shout. If you don't stand still, I find you in three weeks and you won't be interesting any more.
beats.ch04.s01.b015: Dec hops into his waders and catches Inès's eye.
beats.ch04.s01.b016: Your mother's hairdresser has a very complete family.
beats.ch04.s02.b001: Black brick, dripping. A hundred metres in, a low gap half hidden by rubble. La Taupe lies on her back and slides into it feet first, like a letter into a postbox.
beats.ch04.s02.b003: Inès goes next, because if she thinks about it she won't.
beats.ch04.s03.b001: A crawl through yellow rock opens into a gallery as tall as a church nave. Pale limestone sweating with damp, black water round their ankles.
beats.ch04.s03.b004: The street above us. They dug out the stone to build Paris, and every gallery is named for the street on top. Up there, someone's eating a kebab.
beats.ch04.s03.b005: Behind them Dec crawls out, stands up, and hits his head on a ceiling exactly as tall as he is not.
beats.ch04.s03.b007: Ow. No, it's fine. It's grand. I'm not complaining.
beats.ch04.s03.b009: He's Irish. It's how they say thank you.
beats.ch04.s03.b010: They walk for an hour. Inès loses her sense of direction in ten minutes. La Taupe talks the whole way.
beats.ch04.s03.b011: Spinoza was badly treated by everyone. Including Spinoza.
beats.ch04.s03.b012: And drainage. Nobody respects drainage. It's the most important art in Paris.
beats.ch04.s03.b013: Is that you and Spinoza on the drainage side, or...
beats.ch04.s03.b015: They wade to the knees twice. In one gallery Dec has to turn sideways and hold his breath, and not one complaint comes out of him. Inès finds herself almost sorry.
beats.ch04.s04.b001: The walls change. Long brown bones stacked like firewood, ends outward, and set into the stack at chest height a row of skulls, all looking the same way.
beats.ch04.s04.b003: The overflow. When they emptied the old cemeteries, the tourist part filled up. The rest went wherever there was room. The old tollgate's right above us.
beats.ch04.s04.b004: Inès has cleaned the faces of martyrs and a Flemish field of plague dead. This is different. The skulls all face one way, patient, as if waiting for a bus.
beats.ch04.s04.b006: Along the walls of bone, at intervals, arched hollows a metre high, each with a stone sill. Some hold a scratched cross. One holds a jam jar with a dead flower in it.
beats.ch04.s04.b008: They count. La Taupe counts with them out loud, in French, as if counting sheep.
beats.ch04.s04.b010: The ninth is empty. No cross, no jar. Smooth stone sill, smooth sides, a back wall of yellow limestone.
beats.ch04.s04.b011: Dec puts his hand flat on the back wall and moves it slowly, the way Inès runs her fingertips over a canvas to feel where the paint changes. He stops. He pushes.
beats.ch04.s04.b012: Deep in the rock, something goes clunk, like a big key turning in a big door. The back of the niche swings inward.
beats.ch04.s04.b014: For the first time tonight she sounds about twelve.
beats.ch04.s05.b001: A round room cut from the rock, the size of the atelier, under a low dome. The floor is dry and swept. Nine tall empty niches stand round the walls, each with a little stone step in front, like a place for a person to stand.
beats.ch04.s05.b004: On the altar, on a wooden stand, lies a ledger bound in leather the colour of dried blood.
beats.ch04.s05.b005: Inès goes to it before she can think, and turns the pages with the end of her pencil, as in an archive.
beats.ch04.s05.b006: The first half is old. Brown ink, the hands changing every few pages. Horae solutae. Heures payées. Hours paid.
beats.ch04.s05.b007: The second half is new. Black ink. One neat hand. And a different heading.
beats.ch04.s05.b009: And under it, the ink so new it still seems wet:
beats.ch04.s05.b011: The judge. The bookseller. The curate. Roux. Pichon's four cases.
beats.ch04.s05.b012: And Lassalle. No hour after his name. Just remis. Delivered. Returned. Paid off.
beats.ch04.s05.b014: Somebody wrote him off. In a book. Like a bill.
beats.ch04.s05.b015: At the bottom of the page, set apart from the names, a note in the same neat hand.
beats.ch04.s05.b017: By the rule of the Debt Clock. Brother Anselm Vey. The Priory of Combe-Noire, in the Jura.
beats.ch04.s05.b018: Vey. The man who made Roux's lock. Roux said it: Vey kept the word in his book.
beats.ch04.s06.b001: Far off down the galleries, getting nearer: footsteps in water. Many of them, slow and even.
beats.ch04.s06.b002: And voices, low, rising and falling. It takes Inès a breath to understand. They are chanting.
beats.ch04.s06.b004: There's nowhere to run. Only the niches. The one behind the altar is deepest. In, all of us, and not a sound.
beats.ch04.s06.b005: The cataphiles who see things down here are the ones they never find.
beats.ch04.s06.b006: A light flickers far down the gallery. Candles, moving in pairs.
beats.ch04.s06.b007: Dec stays where he is, eyes on the ledger: Roux's name, and the word after Lassalle's.
beats.ch04.s06.b008: Whoever wrote that is about to walk through that door. And we'd be in a hole, in the dark, not even knowing his face.
beats.ch04.s06.b009: Roux said silver hair. A voice like warm oil. A watch with no hands. One look under the hood and we'd have a face to give Pichon.
beats.ch04.s06.b010: One look and they look back. I know these galleries. You don't.
beats.ch04.s06.b011: Keep that lamp on and you're on your own. I don't wait for anybody.
beats.ch04.s06.b013: Tell me to switch it off and I will.
beats.ch04.s06.b014: The footsteps reach the bone wall outside. The candlelight finds the edge of the open stone door.
beats.ch04.s06.b015: Inès's thumb is on the switch of her headlamp. Dec's lamp is still burning, pointed at the door.
beats.ch04.s06.b016: She has known La Taupe for one hour. She has known Dec for three days.
beats.ch05.s01.b001: Three people pressed into a hollow of cold stone, the stone door pulled almost shut. Inès feels Dec's heart hammering through his jacket.
beats.ch05.s01.b002: The door swings open. Candlelight spills in.
beats.ch05.s01.b004: Inès counts. Eighteen. Eight pairs stop on the stone steps in front of eight niches. The ninth pair goes on to the altar.
beats.ch05.s01.b005: The niche with three idiots in waders pressed into the back of it, they leave empty.
beats.ch05.s01.b006: The chanting stops. Somebody at the altar turns the pages of the ledger.
beats.ch05.s01.b008: A man's voice, quiet, cultivated. Someone who has never had to shout, because people lean closer to hear him.
beats.ch05.s01.b009: Warm oil. Roux said a voice like warm oil.
beats.ch05.s01.b010: He was afraid. Fear is a debt like any other. He has paid it. Pray for him.
beats.ch05.s01.b011: Brothers. Our restorer is close to the word. Our clocks are ready.
beats.ch05.s01.b012: In seven days the moon will cover the sun. At the hour of None the voice from Allouis will speak for us, and the city will hear its debt called in.
beats.ch05.s01.b013: And the Seventh will collect. Mutuo datum.
beats.ch05.s01.b015: Given as a loan. It shall be repaid.
beats.ch05.s01.b016: Our restorer. Our restorer is close to the word.
beats.ch05.s01.b017: In the dark, Dec's hand finds hers. She grips it hard enough to hurt them both.
beats.ch05.s01.b018: The candles go out pair by pair, the chant fading down the galleries. The last pair stops in the doorway to pull the stone door shut. One of them is far larger than the other.
beats.ch05.s01.b020: The door closes. On the other side, a heavy iron sound, like a bolt going home.
beats.ch05.s02.b002: We're locked in a cult's bedroom under the fourteenth and nobody knows we're here.
beats.ch05.s02.b004: He puts his whole long body against the stone door. It won't move a whisper. His lamp swings round the walls, and stops.
beats.ch05.s02.b006: Dec unrolls the cutlery on the chapel floor like he is laying a table for Sunday dinner. His hands are shaking. By the second pick, they are not.
beats.ch05.s02.b007: Old lever lock. Two levers. Not been opened since Napoleon was a boy. She's going to be a right...
beats.ch05.s02.b008: The lock makes a noise like a kicked gate.
beats.ch05.s02.b010: Drainage. Eighteenth century. Mon Dieu, it's beautiful. Follow me exactly. Exactly.
beats.ch05.s03.b002: Wet to the neck, all three of them start to laugh, so hard that a light comes on in a window above.
beats.ch05.s03.b003: Inès laughs until it turns into something else, and then back. She wipes her glasses on the inside of her collar.
beats.ch05.s03.b007: Professional reasons. It's Vey's lock. If his clock's in the Jura, his lock's in the Jura, and I want to see it.
beats.ch05.s04.b001: Grey suburbs give way to green fields.
beats.ch05.s04.b003: My father was a locksmith in Galway forty years. Hartley and Son on the van in red, before there was a son to speak of.
beats.ch05.s04.b004: He used to say every lock's a story about what somebody's afraid of. Three deadbolts on an empty flat, he's not afraid of burglars. He's afraid of someone in particular.
beats.ch05.s04.b005: He died in twenty-one. Turns out I'm a very good locksmith and a very bad businessman. Somebody's painted the van white and does plumbing in it.
beats.ch05.s04.b006: So. Escape rooms. You build a story about being afraid, and people pay to get out.
beats.ch05.s04.b007: He looks up. She is watching him over her glasses.
beats.ch05.s04.b008: Sorry. I talk. It's a thing.
beats.ch05.s05.b001: A thin young man in a long grey coat steps off their train three carriages down, glances at the board, and looks away very quickly at nothing.
beats.ch05.s05.b004: She looks round. Of course she does.
beats.ch05.s05.b005: The chain on his waistcoat. I'll bet you the rest of this pretzel there's a watch on it with no hands.
beats.ch05.s05.b006: I don't want the rest of your pretzel. Platform four. Walk normally.
beats.ch05.s05.b008: You walk like a stepladder somebody's trying to carry.
beats.ch05.s06.b001: The young man in grey sits at the far end of the carriage behind a Swiss newspaper.
beats.ch05.s06.b003: He's been on the same page since Basel. Pharmaceutical share prices. That's not a share-prices face.
beats.ch05.s06.b004: Then stop looking at him. You are less discreet than the mountains.
beats.ch05.s06.b005: Her phone buzzes. She reads it, goes still, and turns the screen to him.
beats.ch05.s06.b008: I took it off his card while he was eating.
beats.ch05.s06.b009: She types with one finger: I am with my mother. Sends it. Puts the phone face down.
beats.ch05.s06.b010: Nine minutes of nine o'clock, in a station at rush hour. And the warm-oil fella said our restorer. Like you're theirs.
beats.ch05.s06.b012: At the far end of the carriage the choirboy turns a page. It is the same page.
beats.ch05.s07.b001: Farmhouses with roofs almost to the ground, an onion-spired church. High on the hill, a square black tower and a broken wall.
beats.ch05.s07.b004: I told you to bring boots.
beats.ch05.s07.b005: I'm from Galway. We don't have weather. We have rain.
beats.ch05.s07.b006: The young man in grey walks past close enough to touch. As his coat swings, Dec sees the round edge of a watch in the waistcoat pocket.
beats.ch05.s07.b007: He walks up the single street, turns in at a gate, and is gone.
