beats.ch08.s06.b009: The van swings round a hairpin. The crates slide, and she slides with them against him, and stays.
beats.ch08.s06.b010: I was frightened. When he took my hand to open the phone. I've never been so frightened in my life.
beats.ch08.s06.b011: Inès says something in Hungarian, low and quick.
beats.ch08.s06.b013: Nothing. It's Hungarian. It doesn't count.
beats.ch08.s06.b014: In the dark her hand finds the sleeve of his jacket, and holds on all the way down the mountain.
beats.ch09.s01.b001: Morel has a rule about Sundays. But the skylight is lit, and the Allegory of the Sundial stands on the easel under Inès's UV lamp.
beats.ch09.s01.b003: He is working on the gap in the Latin line. Too deep, too fast, too much solvent, right where the painter's ghost ticks lie in the ground.
beats.ch09.s01.b004: Jean-Paul. Stop. You're taking off the ground.
beats.ch09.s01.b005: The scalpel goes skittering across the floor. His face is grey and wet.
beats.ch09.s01.b006: Inès. You said a week. Your family.
beats.ch09.s01.b008: She has had a list ready since Basel, beginning with the flyleaf. She doesn't need it. He puts his face in his hands and cries, the way a tap drips.
beats.ch09.s01.b009: She switches off the UV lamp, pulls up the other stool and waits.
beats.ch09.s01.b010: The gallery, in two thousand and nineteen. My partner went to Brazil, then came the virus. Three banks. My wife still thinks the flat in Vincennes is ours.
beats.ch09.s01.b011: Then Lassalle came. My notary for years. He had a client, a patron of the arts, who would buy my debts. For a few small favours.
beats.ch09.s01.b013: Morel flinches as if she has hit him.
beats.ch09.s01.b014: A valuation. A painting lent for a party. Then last autumn they asked if I still remembered my radio.
beats.ch09.s01.b015: As a boy I built long-wave transmitters in my father's shed in Brittany. I told Lassalle once, at dinner, as a joke.
beats.ch09.s01.b016: They gave me figures to check. Power, frequency, range. A son et lumière, they said. I wrote my name in the front of the notebook like a schoolboy.
beats.ch09.s01.b017: I didn't ask what it was for. That's what I was paid for. Not to ask.
beats.ch09.s01.b019: They need a word under the varnish for their ceremony on the first. I'm a businessman with a diploma, Inès. I can't see what you see. So I gave it to you.
beats.ch09.s01.b020: You'd find the word, I'd take it to them, and you'd never know. Nobody would be hurt.
beats.ch09.s01.b021: Gérard Lassalle is in the river. Anselme Roux lost a day.
beats.ch09.s01.b022: I know! On Friday a young man telephoned. Very polite. He said Lassalle was afraid at the end, and fear is a debt like any other.
beats.ch09.s01.b023: He hoped I wasn't afraid. They expect the word by Sunday night.
beats.ch09.s01.b026: She believes him. She tells him nothing about the tower, or REMIT, or the R and the E in her notebook.
beats.ch09.s01.b027: Four floors down, the street bell rings. A long, polite, unhurried ring. Morel goes the colour of old paper.
beats.ch09.s02.b001: Even footsteps climb all four flights, and the man who reaches the top has lost no breath. He looks round the room like someone who has paid for it.
beats.ch09.s02.b003: Madame Varga. Forgive me for coming on a Sunday. Auguste de Vaulmont.
beats.ch09.s02.b004: The voice is warm oil, poured slowly. She last heard it under the Barrière d'Enfer, saying Lassalle has been remitted.
beats.ch09.s02.b006: Her own voice comes out quite normal. She will be proud of that later.
beats.ch09.s02.b007: I've come for the Allegory. It's needed for the vigil on Wednesday. My people are downstairs with a van.
beats.ch09.s02.b008: He stands before the painting, hands behind his back, and looks at the square of blue sky she uncovered.
beats.ch09.s02.b009: You have very good hands. I've owned this picture thirty years and never knew the sky was that colour.
beats.ch09.s02.b011: The owner. Poor Gérard loved his little fictions. I asked him for the best hands in Paris, and he found them.
beats.ch09.s02.b012: You were in the mountains, I think. The air on the plateau is very clear in March. One can hear bells for miles.
beats.ch09.s02.b013: In her apron pockets, her hands close into fists.
beats.ch09.s02.b014: I knew your father a little. Zoltán Varga. He drove the twenty-eight in Lyon, past the Hôtel-Dieu, and sang in Hungarian at red lights. A fine baritone.
beats.ch09.s02.b015: To lose one's days like that, one by one. The cruellest debt is the one we pay without knowing we owe it.
beats.ch09.s02.b016: Inès stands quite still. He hasn't said a word a stranger could call a threat. He has simply told her what he holds.
beats.ch09.s02.b017: Your Monsieur Hartley is building us a charming room. I do hope nothing interrupts his contract.
beats.ch09.s02.b018: And Jean-Paul's affairs are so complicated. This atelier is mortgaged to a bank on whose board I sit.
beats.ch09.s02.b019: We all hold a little of each other's time, Madame Varga. We're all in debt to someone.
beats.ch09.s02.b020: He opens his silver watch, the way any man checks the time, and looks into it.
beats.ch09.s02.b024: No. I don't suppose you did.
beats.ch09.s03.b001: Two men in grey overalls carry the painting down in blankets. A van waits with its back doors open.
beats.ch09.s03.b003: Brother Kessler will take it from here. He's very good with fragile things.
beats.ch09.s03.b004: Kessler lifts the painting into the van as gently as if it were asleep. Vaulmont gets into a long dark car and is gone.
beats.ch09.s03.b005: Inès has forty-one photographs, in the cloud and on a memory stick in her coat. She has nine ticks, an R, an E, and REMIT. She doesn't have the painting.
beats.ch09.s03.b007: Go home. Lock your door. Don't drink anything anyone gives you.
beats.ch09.s04.b001: She rang him at ten, at half past and at eleven. Then she rang Dec, who came on a hired bicycle in nineteen minutes. The door wasn't locked.
beats.ch09.s04.b003: On the low table sit a cup and saucer, with a finger's depth of cold tea.
beats.ch09.s04.b008: His tongue is grey, much darker than Roux's.
beats.ch09.s04.b009: Dec is already on the phone to the emergency services, spelling the address twice in his terrible French.
beats.ch09.s04.b010: They aren't angry with him. It's housekeeping. A debt that stopped being useful, written off.
beats.ch09.s04.b011: And now they've one restorer left.
beats.ch09.s04.b013: Dec rings off. The next number in his phone says Commissaire Pichon.
beats.ch09.s04.b014: Pichon would want to know about this.
beats.ch09.s04.b015: Pichon answers to the prefect. And the prefect is on Fabien's list, Dec. He's drinking the wine on Wednesday.
beats.ch09.s04.b016: Pichon also fed me a cassoulet and let me go.
beats.ch09.s04.b017: In the armchair, Morel stares at the wall. On the mantelpiece the carriage clock says nine and stays there.
beats.ch10.s01.b001: Fourth floor of a glass building. On the desk, an andouillette that smells like a farmyard that has been through something.
beats.ch10.s01.b003: Dec tells him everything, from the chapel to Vincennes. Pichon stops chewing only once, at the Seventh will collect. Inès puts her phone and a memory stick on the desk. He reads one photograph twice.
beats.ch10.s01.b005: Morel is at the Hôtel-Dieu. He doesn't know his name. Datura, much more than the others. He may come back. He may not.
beats.ch10.s01.b006: And Lassalle. Datura in the blood, water in the lungs. He was alive when he went into the Seine. Marks on his arms where two hands held him. Large hands.
beats.ch10.s01.b008: On Sunday the prefect's office telephoned. Very politely. The prefect expects the heart attack to be confirmed.
beats.ch10.s01.b009: He'll be at the vigil, as guest of a friend. Whose foundation complains of an Irishman trespassing in Switzerland.
beats.ch10.s01.b010: Your name is on a list, Monsieur Hartley. Not my list. Theirs.
beats.ch10.s02.b003: Declan Hartley. You are under arrest for obstruction of a criminal inquiry. Stand up.
beats.ch10.s02.b005: Sit down, Madame Varga, or you will join him.
beats.ch10.s02.b006: He walks Dec slowly past every desk. By the lifts, a man in a good suit who doesn't look like a policeman holds a coffee, watches them go by, and takes out his phone.
beats.ch10.s02.b007: In the lift Pichon lets go of his arm and watches the numbers go down, his face grey and old.
beats.ch10.s03.b001: A bench, a steel toilet, frosted glass. A steel door with a card reader. No keyhole.
beats.ch10.s03.b004: Everybody does. It was designed by a man who had never been arrested. I'm sorry for upstairs.
beats.ch10.s03.b005: The man by the lifts is the prefect's. For perhaps a day, they'll think I know which way the wind blows.
beats.ch10.s03.b006: On paper you were released at one. I'll sign after my dessert.
beats.ch10.s03.b008: I believed you on the first day. When you told me about the tongue.
beats.ch10.s03.b009: But if I go upstairs with photographs of a notebook I don't have and a sermon about a monk, they take my badge. Then there's no one.
beats.ch10.s03.b010: He holds out a folded sheet of paper.
beats.ch10.s03.b011: A police officer reads a great many boring documents. Sometimes he leaves them lying about.
beats.ch10.s03.b013: The pendulum hangs from the crown of the dome. Sixty-seven metres of cable. A fine thing to hang other things from, if one were a radio amateur from Brittany.
beats.ch10.s03.b014: I know nothing about radios. I know about lunch. There's a tarte Tatin in the canteen, and I've had a difficult morning. Mind the door. It's heavy.
beats.ch10.s03.b015: His shoes go away up the stairs. The steel door stands wide open, its card reader blinking. Dec had very nearly worked that reader out.
beats.ch10.s03.b016: That's not fair. I'd have had that.
beats.ch10.s04.b002: The pendulum cable. It's a sixty-seven-metre aerial hanging in the middle of Paris.
beats.ch10.s04.b003: And I'm on a list. If the prefecture sees me near the Panthéon on Wednesday, I'm done.
beats.ch10.s04.b004: His phone buzzes. He reads the email and starts to laugh, quite helplessly.
beats.ch10.s04.b007: Where he can see me. In the crypt, in a little room I built with a door that locks, while he's up under the dome with his radio.
beats.ch10.s04.b008: Nobody arrests a man Vaulmont put on his own guest list. The pass is the trap, and it's the door. And I know every way out of that room. I drew them.
beats.ch10.s05.b001: One lamp on the bench, orange cloud in the skylight. Dec is asleep on the green sofa with his boots on, talking.
beats.ch10.s05.b002: Ah, Mrs Kilbride, sure it's no trouble.
beats.ch10.s05.b004: Under the lamp: photograph twenty-three, her notebook, the REMIT page, Roux's drawings.
beats.ch10.s05.b005: Ne csak nézd, lásd. Don't just look. See.
beats.ch10.s05.b007: Not decoration. A table. Count round each wheel from its own first letter.
beats.ch10.s05.b008: She counts like stitches. Seventeen on the first wheel: R. Four on the second, which starts at B: E.
beats.ch10.s05.b010: The ninth gate has no number. Only a blank square, and Roux's furious biro.
beats.ch10.s05.b012: She turns to photograph twenty-three. Nine ghost ticks, and at the foot of the ninth a short flat stroke. E or L. No word ends remitterl.
beats.ch10.s05.b014: To send back. To let go. To forgive a debt.
beats.ch10.s05.b015: Mutuo datum remittere hora nona. What was given as a loan, to forgive at the ninth hour.
beats.ch10.s05.b016: Not reddetur. Not repaid. Vey wrote the other word, and made it the word for his lock.
beats.ch10.s05.b017: Their own lock says forgive. And in six hundred years they never counted round the letters.
beats.ch10.s05.b018: She takes off her glasses, presses her hands to her eyes, and puts them back. Then she kicks the sofa.
beats.ch10.s05.b020: Get up. I've got the word.
beats.ch10.s06.b002: That's mad. You did that with a pencil.
beats.ch10.s06.b003: Don't make a thing of it.
beats.ch10.s06.b004: And Roux's copy, up in the dome on the radio, opens with the same word. I was going to pick it.
beats.ch10.s06.b005: Vey cut by candlelight. Roux had a lathe and a grudge. I'd be there till Easter.
beats.ch10.s07.b002: Soufflot found the hill full of holes and nearly had a heart attack. An old gallery under the rue Clotilde runs up to the east end of the crypt.
beats.ch10.s07.b003: To a shaft with a grille nobody's opened in two hundred years. It comes up in a little chapel off the crypt.
beats.ch10.s07.b004: The north-east chapel. That's where they're putting my room.
beats.ch10.s07.b005: That afternoon, four metres up a brick shaft, Inès clings to the rungs and doesn't look down. Through the rusted bars: the underside of pale new planks, stamped in blue by a timber yard in Montreuil.
beats.ch10.s07.b006: That's my floor. They've built my room right on top of their own back door.
beats.ch10.s07.b007: I'll open it tomorrow, from the top. Nobody'll need it. But I like to know there's a way out.
beats.ch10.s08.b001: Mademoiselle Ferrand answered Inès in twelve minutes: of course the restorer may stay with her painting. Monsieur de Vaulmont would be delighted.
beats.ch10.s08.b003: We're both inside, with a word for a lock in the roof and a back door in the cellar. And then what?
beats.ch10.s08.b004: You look at the door. I look at the painting. We see what's wrong.
beats.ch11.s01.b001: A trolley of three wooden crates, stencilled FRAGILE and CECI N'EST PAS UNE BOMBE. It seemed funny in the workshop in February.
beats.ch11.s01.b003: Escape room. For the guests. Pour s'amuser.
beats.ch11.s01.b004: The stencil's a joke. Magritte? The pipe?
beats.ch11.s01.b005: Nobody wants to argue about Magritte at seven in the morning. The guard waves him through.
beats.ch11.s02.b001: Pale stone, columns like oak trees, a dome so high its saints are the size of thumbnails. From the crown a steel cable comes down sixty-seven metres to a brass sphere swinging above a brass ring.
beats.ch11.s02.b003: Beside it stand a low grey stage, a lectern, and an easel under grey cloth.
beats.ch11.s02.b005: They look at each other across the nave. Neither moves. The pendulum swings between them, and back.
beats.ch11.s03.b001: His room: stone-effect walls, a bench of brass gears, a real iron lock. On the wall, a clock with nine hours on its face. The client's brief asked for it. He thought it was a quirk.
beats.ch11.s03.b003: Through the hatch in his planks he reaches the old iron grille. Its lock takes nine minutes. He can't stop counting in nines.
beats.ch11.s03.b004: The bolt goes back. He leaves the grille closed but unlocked, and puts the hatch back.
beats.ch11.s03.b005: Nobody'll need it. But it's there.
beats.ch11.s04.b001: A hard blue sky, but the light has gone wrong, every shadow thin and slightly blue. Outside, hundreds hold up cardboard eclipse glasses.
beats.ch11.s04.b002: Inside: a tall tired minister, the prefect of police in silver braid, two bankers in navy, a priest with a purple sash, a presenter with a famous tan.
beats.ch11.s04.b004: Everyone Vaulmont speaks to walks away a little straighter, as if something has been lent to them.
beats.ch11.s04.b006: She doesn't look at Dec. That's the arrangement. Once, as the pendulum swings between them, her eyes meet his and go back to her clipboard.
beats.ch11.s05.b001: Agency waiters, young and bored. At the back table, a man in a white jacket that doesn't suit him, with a narrow back Dec would know anywhere.
beats.ch11.s05.b003: Steel urns of ordinary vin chaud. And apart, four pewter jugs of something almost brown, with a grey sheen like the bloom on a plum.
beats.ch11.s05.b005: The whole chapel smells of cloves.
beats.ch11.s05.b006: Dec turns away before Fabien can turn round, and walks straight into a waiter with a tray of spoons.
beats.ch11.s05.b008: Pardon, monsieur. Ça va? You're white.
beats.ch11.s05.b010: Moussa. The brown wine in the pewter. When does it go out?
beats.ch11.s05.b011: Half past two. Only the guests on his list. Any waiter who drinks it is sacked.
beats.ch11.s05.b012: It smells like a church at Christmas. This morning I saw him tip something into the jugs from a paper bag. Grey, like ash.
beats.ch11.s05.b013: It's a drug. It makes you lose a day, and remember only what you're told.
beats.ch11.s05.b014: Then the minister and the prefect say it on the telly.
beats.ch11.s05.b015: I need to swap the jugs and keep the real ones for the police. I can't do it on my own.
beats.ch11.s05.b016: How much do you think I'm paid for this?
beats.ch11.s05.b018: Eleven euros forty an hour. Before tax. And he shouted at Fatou for folding the napkins wrong.
beats.ch11.s06.b001: A crate stencilled CECI N'EST PAS UNE BOMBE stands by the wall. Moussa knocks it over with great force and theatrical surprise.
beats.ch11.s06.b002: Four hundred brass gears burst out and ring across the stone, like all the coins in the world dropped at once.
beats.ch11.s06.b004: Every waiter goes down on hands and knees. For forty seconds every eye is on the floor.
beats.ch11.s06.b005: Dec builds rooms where forty seconds is a whole puzzle.
beats.ch11.s06.b006: Behind the screen, the four pewter jugs go into the empty crate. In their place go four jugs of Moussa's vin chaud, a spoonful of cocoa stirred into each. Brown-grey and dull. Under a lid, it will do.
beats.ch11.s06.b007: Dec shuts the crate and sits on it.
beats.ch11.s06.b008: Fabien stands up with his hands full of brass. The jugs are where they always were. Moussa apologises at length, in French and Wolof.
beats.ch11.s07.b002: The silver trays go out. The guests on the list look at the little clock on the cup, smile, and drink.
beats.ch11.s07.b003: Across the nave, Vaulmont's calm face relaxes very slightly, like a man hearing the last wheel of a lock fall into place.
beats.ch11.s08.b001: The sun is a thin sickle behind the moon. The light drains as if someone is turning down a dimmer on Paris.
beats.ch11.s08.b004: The voice fills the nave. Warm oil, poured slowly.
beats.ch11.s08.b005: Every hour of every life is lent. Today, for a few minutes, the light that measures our hours will be taken away.
beats.ch11.s08.b006: And we will stand together in the dark, and remember it was never ours to keep.
beats.ch11.s08.b007: Up the south aisle comes a thin pale figure in a white jacket, scanning the columns.
beats.ch11.s08.b009: The narrow face finds his and stays blank. Fabien's lips move, into the earpiece.
beats.ch11.s08.b010: At the foot of the roped stair, Kessler's great bald head turns slowly toward the south aisle.
beats.ch11.s08.b011: Dec can't go up now. Every step he takes, two men will take with him.
beats.ch11.s08.b012: He looks across the nave for Inès. She has already put her clipboard down on the easel.
beats.ch11.s09.b001: Inès walks the north aisle without hurrying, in her green dress and mustard scarf. Nobody watches a woman with a clipboard, or notices she has left it behind.
beats.ch11.s09.b003: Behind it is the other stair, the service stair inside the wall: sixty metres round and round, a greasy rope for a handrail and nothing on the other side.
beats.ch11.s09.b004: It is the stair she is most afraid of.
beats.ch11.s09.b005: Up there, where the pendulum cable meets the crown, waits the transmitter from Morel's notebook.
beats.ch11.s09.b006: She looks back once and finds Dec behind his column. He can't nod. Fabien is watching him.
beats.ch11.s09.b008: She puts her hand on the rope and looks up into the dark.
beats.ch12.s01.b001: A stone spiral barely wider than her shoulders. A greasy rope for a handrail. On the inner side, a hand's-width gap and darkness dropping away.
beats.ch12.s01.b003: She doesn't look down. She counts, the way she counted Vey's wheels. One step, one number.
beats.ch12.s01.b005: By a hundred the stair has begun to tilt. She presses her forehead to cold stone and shuts her eyes.
beats.ch12.s01.b007: At nine she froze on the first landing of a tower in Lyon. Her father sat beside her, sang a long song about a horse, asked: up or down? She said down.
beats.ch12.s01.b009: She opens her eyes and climbs.
beats.ch12.s02.b001: A narrow stone ring, a waist-high balustrade, sixty metres of darkening air below. The pendulum's sphere a pinhead. The steel cable rises past her to the crown; from the crown a second cable, black and new, runs down the dome's ribs.
beats.ch12.s02.b003: A hum she feels in her teeth.
beats.ch12.s02.b004: ...and when the light is taken from us, my friends, we will see what we truly owe...
beats.ch12.s02.b005: She walks to it with her hand on the wall, giving the drop nothing. Roux's wheels are crisp, perfect. She steadies her wrist, as for gold leaf on a halo, and turns the first.
beats.ch12.s02.b007: Behind her, from the south stair, footsteps.
beats.ch12.s03.b002: He comes on slowly, the way you follow a cat you don't want to frighten into the road. She backs away round the ring, shaking from her teeth to her knees.
beats.ch12.s03.b003: ...nine minutes, my friends. Only nine. The hour of None...
beats.ch12.s03.b004: Below, a hundred voices gasp. Outside, thousands. A long rising sigh, like wind through trees.
beats.ch12.s04.b001: The dome turns a deep glowing blue, the inside of a mussel shell, a ring of pale fire in the windows.
beats.ch12.s04.b002: Through the great doors, the traffic lights of the rue Soufflot flash red again.
beats.ch12.s04.b005: Something explodes into her face. Wings, dust. Her hip hits the balustrade; for one endless second there is nothing on her right but blue dark. Then she is on her knees, arms round a baluster.
beats.ch12.s04.b007: For a few seconds the sixty metres vanish. Something is more frightened than she is. She folds its wings under her palm and works the mesh free. Her hand shakes. The bird lets her.
beats.ch12.s04.b008: Kessler has stopped two metres away, his head turned toward the bird. She holds it out to him in both hands, palm up, the way he held out his hand for the notebook in the tower.
beats.ch12.s04.b010: His hands are very warm. He stands with the bird against his chest, still as a man in church, and she walks past him. Then she runs.
beats.ch12.s04.b011: At the far stairhead a torch beam swings up out of the arch, and Dec behind it, gasping.
beats.ch12.s04.b013: The cabinet! It's Roux's lock. You can't pick it. Use the word!
beats.ch12.s04.b014: The torch finds the nine wheels. And behind Dec, coming up out of the same arch, unhurried, a small dark pistol in one gloved hand: Vaulmont.
beats.ch12.s04.b015: Inès doesn't stop. A low iron door in the east pier opens on a conservators' stair, down to the nave, the microphone, the painting.
beats.ch12.s04.b016: You look at the door. I look at the painting.
beats.ch12.s04.b017: She takes the steps two at a time into the dark.
beats.ch12.s05.b002: Monsieur Hartley. Please don't touch that. Monsieur Roux is a genius, and a very rude one. You could be there with your picks until Easter.
beats.ch12.s05.b004: In four minutes the debt is called. Afterwards nothing bad will happen to you. We are not monsters. We simply keep accounts.
beats.ch12.s05.b005: Dec doesn't step away. When he's frightened, he talks.
beats.ch12.s05.b006: Can I tell you something about locks? My da used to say every lock's a story about what somebody's afraid of.
beats.ch12.s05.b007: Behind his back his fingers find the first wheel. Already on R. The second: four, from B. They went over the offsets thirty times at the bench.
beats.ch12.s05.b008: This one's a monk in a plague. Built a whole religion on everyone owing everyone. And he's terrified. Of his own bill.
beats.ch12.s05.b009: So he puts in his lock the one word he wants and doesn't think he'll get. And you lot keep his nine numbers six hundred years like a relic.
beats.ch12.s05.b011: And not one banker or bishop among you ever counted round the letters.
beats.ch12.s05.b014: There is no word. There are numbers. The Rule...
beats.ch12.s05.b015: Seventh. Eighth. All those people, to find a word that was in your lock the whole time.
beats.ch12.s05.b016: It's not pay, Monsieur de Vaulmont.
beats.ch12.s05.b020: A small, deep, perfect click. The brass doors swing open an inch, the hum comes out loud, the green light.
beats.ch12.s05.b022: He turns it, hard, all the way round, until it clunks. The green lights go out down the rack. Silence fills the dome.
beats.ch12.s05.b023: Vaulmont stares at the wheels. His lips move, spelling the word letter by letter, like a child.
beats.ch12.s05.b024: Below, the traffic lights of the rue Soufflot turn green. The FONDATION VAULMONT clock lurches, sweeps round, stops.
beats.ch12.s05.b026: Two minutes short of None. A puzzled murmur goes through the nave: people promised a miracle, watching it tidy itself away.
beats.ch12.s05.b027: Then a woman's voice comes out of the loudspeakers.
beats.ch12.s06.b001: Far below, in the TV light, a small figure in a mustard scarf pulls the cloth off the painting and holds photograph twenty-three to the camera.
beats.ch12.s06.b002: My name is Inès Varga. I restore this painting. This is their founder's last line. Someone scraped one word out. I've put it back.
beats.ch12.s06.b003: Mutuo datum remittere hora nona. What was given as a loan, forgive at the ninth hour.
beats.ch12.s06.b004: And the clocks were not a miracle. There's a transmitter in the dome, built by the Fondation Vaulmont. Someone has just turned it off.
beats.ch12.s06.b005: The wine you drank at half past two was meant to hold datura. It was swapped. The real wine is in a crate in the south transept.
beats.ch12.s06.b006: In the silence, sixty metres up, Dec hears the pendulum go past.
beats.ch12.s06.b007: The minister, empty pewter cup in hand, begins to laugh helplessly. The prefect has gone the colour of a church candle. The camera's red light stays on.
beats.ch12.s06.b008: Dec turns. Vaulmont has lowered the pistol.
beats.ch12.s06.b011: Vaulmont looks at him with enormous patience, like a man considering a bill. Then he turns the pistol round and holds it out, butt first. Dec takes it like a dead fish.
beats.ch12.s06.b012: I'll go down by the stair. You'll forgive me if I don't wait for you.
beats.ch12.s07.b001: The light returns as a long silver dawn. Outside, the crowd cheers, a little embarrassed by its relief.
beats.ch12.s07.b003: Auguste de Vaulmont. I'm arresting you for the murder of Gérard Lassalle.
beats.ch12.s07.b004: And for poisoning Anselme Roux, Judge Delorme, Madame Aubry, the Abbé Girardin and Jean-Paul Morel. All alive, I'm happy to say, and very angry.
beats.ch12.s07.b005: You like to keep accounts. So do I.
beats.ch12.s07.b006: Kessler comes out of the south stair with his hands empty and holds out his great wrists to the nearest officer, who goes white.
beats.ch12.s07.b007: From the south transept, a crash, a yelp, a delighted young voice.
beats.ch12.s07.b008: Monsieur l'agent! The thin one tried to take the crate. I'm sitting on him. Do you want him?
beats.ch12.s07.b009: A young officer takes the pistol from Dec's fingers like scissors from a child. The pendulum swings past, and back. It never stopped. It kept its own plane while the city turned underneath.
beats.ch12.s07.b011: He lifts his hand, a little, uncertain.
beats.ch12.s07.b012: After a moment, so slightly nobody else in the Panthéon would see it, she lifts hers.
beats.ch13.s01.b001: Two hundred clocks on the walls, and every one of them stopped. Roux stands at the top of a stepladder with a winding key.
beats.ch13.s01.b003: By the door stand Madame Ferré from the bakery and an old lady in a fur hat, who came in uninvited and won't leave.
beats.ch13.s01.b004: I stopped them myself. Get that straight.
beats.ch13.s01.b005: Yesterday at three I'm sitting here with the radio. The radio says the stations have all stopped at nine. Austerlitz, Montparnasse, Gare de Lyon. The traffic lights to the Seine. The hospitals.
beats.ch13.s01.b006: The man on the radio is frightened. So I look at my clocks.
beats.ch13.s01.b007: Not one stopped. Not one of my clocks listens to Allouis, or to anybody. My clocks listen to me.
beats.ch13.s01.b008: So this morning I stop them all. By hand. At nine. To see how it feels to do it to myself.
beats.ch13.s01.b011: He touches the pendulum of the big walnut regulator on the top shelf, and it swings. Then the carriage clock, and the next, and the next, his small spotted hands working along the shelves, a touch or a turn of the key for each.
beats.ch13.s01.b012: At the bottom of the ladder he opens the little door in the longcase, his father's clock, the chalk long wiped away. He gives the pendulum a push, the way you push a child on a swing.
beats.ch13.s01.b013: The ticking comes up from every side like rain starting on a roof. One drop, then a dozen, then all of them, none together.
beats.ch13.s01.b015: The cuckoo over the workshop door shoots out, says cuckoo once, as if clearing its throat, and goes back in.
beats.ch13.s01.b016: Roux listens with his head on one side until he is satisfied.
beats.ch13.s01.b017: There. That's the only miracle I've ever approved of.
beats.ch13.s01.b018: The old lady in the fur hat bursts into tears.
beats.ch13.s02.b001: White cloths, and the same eleven dishes since nineteen fifty-two. Pichon has been awake for thirty hours. He won't discuss the case before the second course, because at present he is not a just man.
beats.ch13.s02.b003: The blanquette comes in a sauce so white and smooth Inès could lay gold leaf on it. Pichon puts down his fork.
beats.ch13.s02.b004: Fabien Ruel has confessed. To everything.
beats.ch13.s02.b005: The tea at the inn, Monsieur Hartley. Madame Aubry. The curate. Monsieur Roux's coffee. Monsieur Morel's tea. The clocks, every time.
beats.ch13.s02.b006: In great detail, with some pride, in the form of a sermon. My sergeant typed for four hours.
beats.ch13.s02.b007: He believes he will be forgiven. He was very struck by the word on the lock.
beats.ch13.s02.b008: Your young waiter is pressing no charges for the bite.
beats.ch13.s02.b011: Also, the Centre des monuments nationaux wants to keep your clockmaker's cell in the crypt until the end of the summer. An educational exhibit. They ask your fee.
beats.ch13.s02.b012: I told them it was very high.
beats.ch13.s02.b013: Dec opens his mouth, and shuts it again.
beats.ch13.s02.b014: Kessler has said nothing at all. I'm told it's his custom. His hands match the marks on Maître Lassalle's arms. That will do.
beats.ch13.s02.b015: He asked one thing last night, through an interpreter. He speaks only Swiss German, and not much of that.
beats.ch13.s02.b016: He asked if someone could check the netting in the dome. For birds.
beats.ch13.s02.b018: She keeps pushing it until she trusts her face again.
beats.ch13.s02.b019: Jean-Paul Morel woke at six this morning at the Hôtel-Dieu. He asked for his wife. Then he asked what day it was, and when they told him, he wept.
beats.ch13.s02.b020: The doctors think he'll be well. He wants to talk to me, at length. And to you, Madame Varga, when you can bear it.
beats.ch13.s02.b021: I told him that might be some time.
beats.ch13.s02.b023: She is surprised to hear herself say it.
beats.ch13.s02.b024: At seven this morning the minister rang the prefect to thank him for his long service and accept his wish to spend more time in Normandy.
beats.ch13.s02.b025: The prefect didn't know he had that wish until seven. He has it now.
beats.ch13.s02.b026: The wine. Four jugs. Datura, clove, and the ash of burnt paper. They're still working out what paper.
beats.ch13.s02.b028: Pichon puts his fork down again. From his raincoat on the back of the chair he takes a small evidence bag and sets it on the cloth between the bread basket and the salt.
beats.ch13.s02.b030: Released at four this morning. Bail of two million euros. The magistrate is a sensible woman. She wished to keep him.
beats.ch13.s02.b031: Paid in full at three fifty-one, from a foundation in Liechtenstein. It didn't exist on Tuesday. It doesn't exist this morning.
beats.ch13.s02.b032: A car was waiting at the quai des Orfèvres. No plane. No train. He has simply gone.
beats.ch13.s02.b033: He left this. They took it from him at the Panthéon with his tie and his belt. At four, he didn't ask for it back.
beats.ch13.s02.b034: Inès opens the back of the watch through the plastic with her thumbnail, the way she did on the Pont de Sully, a week and a lifetime ago. Where Lassalle's watch had nine little wheels, this one has a single engraved line.
beats.ch13.s02.b037: Dec sets his glass down on the cloth very carefully, as if it might go off. At the next table someone laughs. A waiter drops a spoon. In the kitchen, somebody is singing.
beats.ch13.s02.b040: The Swiss searched the forester's house last night. The black notebook and the board were in the stove, half burnt. Vey's ledger was not.
beats.ch13.s02.b041: Fabien says it went to the Seventh. So it went with him.
beats.ch13.s02.b042: One of the others is called the Keeper of the Last Hour. Though I'm told that's a story nuns tell each other in the evenings.
beats.ch13.s02.b043: He slips the bag back into his raincoat.
beats.ch13.s02.b044: I'll keep this. As a reminder. I have a very bad memory.
beats.ch13.s02.b045: Now. The cheese, the tarte Tatin, and nineteen hours of sleep. And neither of you is going to be in the next case of anything. You hear me?
beats.ch13.s02.b047: Pichon, who doesn't believe a word of it, calls for the cheese.
beats.ch13.s03.b002: They've taken the wall down! The commune, this morning. The fire brigade did it. You can see the whole dial from the village. All nine hours.
beats.ch13.s03.b003: Madame Jobin's nephew went up the ladder with a pot of grease and a library book. He's put the old twelve-hour wheel back. The one my sisters took out in sixteen ten.
beats.ch13.s03.b004: It struck four just now. Four times. Not thirteen. The whole valley came out to listen. I cried.
beats.ch13.s03.b005: I've been on the plum brandy since lunch. Is he there? Your not-husband?
beats.ch13.s03.b007: Good. Give him a kiss from me. On the forehead. Don't let him make it into anything.
beats.ch13.s04.b001: Low gold light comes through the skylight and lies across the benches and the jars of pigment like varnish.
beats.ch13.s04.b003: It will be evidence for months, maybe years. But the magistrate agreed that a half-cleaned seventeenth-century canvas can't wait for the courts. Over the cheese, Pichon told Inès: she goes on, under seal. Something in her chest came loose that she hadn't known was tight.
beats.ch13.s04.b004: She won't paint the word back in. A restorer doesn't. She'll stabilise the scrape, clean round it, and leave the gap honest. Anyone who looks properly will see where someone took a knife to the thing they were most afraid of.
beats.ch13.s04.b005: Behind her, Dec kneels at the atelier door with the old lock half out, the one that has stuck every winter for four years. He has been humming for twenty minutes. He is very happy. She can tell from the humming.
beats.ch13.s04.b007: This is a terrible lock. Who put this in? It's a crime against doors. I'm going to put in a five-lever mortice with a...
beats.ch13.s04.b013: But this building has fourteen doors. Every lock is terrible. And I'm going to need somebody who can get into places.
beats.ch13.s04.b014: She turns round. He is sitting back on his heels, mouth a little open, the gold light in his untidy hair.
beats.ch13.s04.b015: It's a job. That's all. It pays very badly.
beats.ch13.s04.b020: Then the grin comes, the whole enormous Galway grin, the one that looked at her through the back window of a police car eleven days ago.
beats.ch13.s04.b021: Ah, go on, then. Purely professionally.
beats.ch13.s04.b023: Four floors down, the street-door bell rings.
beats.ch13.s05.b001: A courier in a motorcycle helmet wouldn't come up, wouldn't say who sent it, and was gone before Dec reached the last flight.
beats.ch13.s05.b003: They look at it without touching it. Then Inès puts on her white cotton gloves, because that's what she does, and slits one edge with her scalpel.
beats.ch13.s05.b007: Across the roofs of the Marais a church bell begins to strike six. She finds herself counting. Beside her, under his breath, in English, Dec is counting too. They both stop at six, and look at each other, and go on looking.
beats.ch13.s05.b008: Well. That's not a partnership. That's an invitation.
beats.ch13.s05.b009: Inès lays the clock face back in its tissue and closes the box. She takes off her gloves and pushes her glasses up with one knuckle.
beats.ch14.s01.b001: La Taupe kills her lamp. Inès's thumb stays on her switch, and she doesn't press it. Dec plants himself in the doorway and holds his beam high down the gallery.
beats.ch14.s01.b003: Putain. T'es un con. Un beau con.
beats.ch14.s01.b004: The chanting stops. The candles stop. Then they come on again, faster.
beats.ch14.s01.b005: Bonsoir, les gars. Je suis... un touriste.
beats.ch14.s01.b007: Inès counts. It's all she has. Eighteen. Tonight they don't take the niches. They make a ring, and the three of them are inside it.
beats.ch14.s01.b008: The biggest hood steps out. A shovel hand lifts Dec's satchel and pulls out the canvas roll.
beats.ch14.s01.b011: The ninth pair reaches the altar. One of them turns.
beats.ch14.s01.b013: Quiet. Cultured. Warm oil, poured slowly.
beats.ch14.s01.b014: You were engaged to build my cell. Not to visit my chapel.
beats.ch14.s01.b016: We know everyone's name. It is the nature of a ledger.
beats.ch14.s01.b017: Dec swings his lamp full on the hood, and Inès's beam joins it. The man doesn't flinch. He lowers the hood himself, as if they had asked politely.
beats.ch14.s01.b019: He draws a watch from the waistcoat and opens it toward them.
beats.ch14.s01.b021: Silver hair. A voice like warm oil. A watch with no hands.
beats.ch14.s01.b023: Look as long as you like, Monsieur Hartley. You won't keep it.
beats.ch14.s01.b024: The bald man lifts the lamp off Dec's head, gently, like taking scissors from a child. Then Inès's. He turns them both to the floor.
beats.ch14.s02.b002: Dec backs until his heels hit stone. He doesn't stop talking.
beats.ch14.s02.b003: Total malentendu. Mauvais virage rue Saint-Jacques. Signalisation pourrie, ici.
beats.ch14.s02.b004: Behind his back, low at the rusted grille, Inès hears the tiniest scratch of steel. One pick, kept up his sleeve.
beats.ch14.s02.b005: Et puisque vous êtes là. La cellule. La porte s'ouvre dedans ou dehors? Dedans pour le drame. Dehors pour les pompiers.
beats.ch14.s02.b007: Scratch. Two hoods near the altar turn toward the sound.
beats.ch14.s02.b008: Inès steps into the candlelight before her knees can vote.
beats.ch14.s02.b011: It's on my painting, under the varnish. Mutuo datum. Donné en prêt. Given as a loan.
beats.ch14.s02.b012: Un prêt demande un prêteur. A lender, a borrower, a contract. Who signed for the city? Who signed for Roux?
beats.ch14.s02.b013: Madame Varga. Jean-Paul told me you were minutieuse. Thorough.
beats.ch14.s02.b014: He is enjoying this. She can hear it: a man who has waited years for someone worth explaining to.
beats.ch14.s02.b015: God signed. He lent the hours. Brother Vey only kept the accounts.
beats.ch14.s02.b016: Datum. Given. Done. Then a hole where somebody took a knife. You've built a church on half a sentence.
beats.ch14.s02.b017: Then you know how the sentence ends.
beats.ch14.s02.b018: Behind her, a small dry click. The grille screams open, and the sound circles the chapel three times.
beats.ch14.s02.b020: La Taupe dives into the black hole headfirst, like a letter into a postbox. Water splashes. Then nothing.
beats.ch14.s02.b021: The bald man's hand closes on Dec's shoulder. It isn't rough. It doesn't need to be.
beats.ch14.s02.b023: A hood moves toward the drain.
beats.ch14.s02.b024: Laissez-la. Qui croirait une cataphile? Elles voient des fantômes ici tous les week-ends.
beats.ch14.s02.b025: Leave her. Who would believe a cataphile? They see ghosts down here every weekend.
beats.ch14.s03.b001: The silver-haired man opens the ledger to the debtors' page and uncaps a fountain pen. The nib whispers.
beats.ch14.s03.b003: A pewter cup passes hand to hand round the ring. Two hoods hold Inès's arms. She clamps her mouth shut. A gloved thumb presses her jaw, almost kindly, until it opens.
beats.ch14.s03.b005: Sweet and dusty. Then flat and mineral at the back of the tongue, like cold wet stone.
beats.ch14.s03.b006: Cloves. Cloves and slate. Roux said cloves.
beats.ch14.s03.b007: Across the ring, Dec swallows, coughs, and finds her eyes.
beats.ch14.s03.b008: Inès. His face. Hold on to his face.
beats.ch14.s03.b009: She looks. Silver hair. Grey eyes. The watch with no hands. She says it over to herself like a phone number.
beats.ch14.s03.b010: Don't be afraid. You owe us only a day.
beats.ch14.s03.b011: The candles go very far away.
beats.ch14.s04.b001: Low sun on the Seine, green-grey water, bare trees at the tip of the Île Saint-Louis. A jogger passes and doesn't look twice.
beats.ch14.s04.b003: Her mouth tastes of slate. She doesn't know why.
beats.ch14.s04.b004: Dec. Dec. Why are we on a bridge?
beats.ch14.s04.b005: What... I don't know. What time is it? We're meeting La Taupe tonight. It's Wednesday.
beats.ch14.s04.b009: Dec licks dry lips. She grabs his chin.
beats.ch14.s04.b011: He looks at her mouth and goes white.
beats.ch14.s04.b012: He rips open the satchel. No pick roll. No cardboard tube of Roux's drawings. No silver watch.
beats.ch14.s04.b013: Gone. The watch. The drawings. Everything.
beats.ch14.s04.b015: He opens his mouth. Nothing comes.
beats.ch14.s04.b016: There was a face. I looked right at it. Silver... something.
beats.ch14.s04.b017: I had it, Inès. I had it, and it's gone.
beats.ch14.s04.b018: She reaches for it too. Candles, a ring of hoods, a face. Where the face should be there is a smooth blank band, like the sundial before the raking light.
beats.ch14.s04.b019: Her phone wakes in her pocket.
beats.ch14.s04.b022: It can't be Friday. It was Wednesday. Where's Thursday?
beats.ch14.s04.b023: She waited for us at the way out. She rang all day Thursday. And we weren't anywhere.
beats.ch14.s04.b024: His phone buzzes. He reads it and holds it out.
beats.ch14.s04.b026: Vaulmont. The fella paying for my cell.
beats.ch14.s04.b027: The skin on Inès's arms rises under her coat. She can't say why.
beats.ch14.s04.b030: Neither of them knows why it makes them want to run.
beats.ch14.s04.b031: Across the river, a church bell starts to strike. Inès counts every stroke without meaning to.
beats.ch15.s01.b001: The white quilt, Roux's drawings, the tray on the bed.
beats.ch15.s01.b003: Spiced. The Swiss put cloves in everything. Roux said something about cloves. Roux says a lot of things.
beats.ch15.s01.b004: It's the cold. That's all it is.
beats.ch15.s01.b005: He drinks it down. His bones are still cold from the tower, so he pours a second and drinks that too.
beats.ch15.s01.b006: Then the room tilts. Gently. Like a boat leaving a quay.
beats.ch15.s01.b007: He puts the cup on the drawings and misses. Tea runs across Vey's nine wheels. He watches it soak in and can't think why it matters.
beats.ch15.s01.b008: He lies back on the quilt. The ceiling is miles away.
beats.ch15.s02.b001: A key turns in the lock. It sounds like it's in another building.
beats.ch15.s02.b003: Dec sees him in pieces, the way you see a street from a train. A hand on a pot. A chair dragged to the cuckoo clock. His own wrist lifted, his watch turned on it, set down again.
beats.ch15.s02.b005: The words come out in the wrong order and lie down.
beats.ch15.s02.b006: Shh. It's all right, Monsieur Hartley.
beats.ch15.s02.b007: Cool fingers press Dec's thumb to his phone. Then the wardrobe creaks, and somebody is drawing on wood.
beats.ch15.s02.b008: At the door Fabien turns, kind and earnest.
beats.ch15.s02.b009: You owe a day, that's all. Everyone does. Mutuo datum.
beats.ch15.s02.b010: The door closes. Dec means to get up. He means it hard. He watches the ceiling go soft at the edges until it's the moon.
beats.ch15.s03.b001: Inès knocked last night at ten and again at eleven, and got nothing. After the tower she thought he was avoiding her. She thought that was fair.
beats.ch15.s03.b002: This morning Madame Jobin hands her the key without a single honeymoon joke.
beats.ch15.s03.b004: There you are. Is it Saturday? I've to meet you for breakfast. We're going to talk about the weather.
beats.ch15.s03.b006: He does, as obliging as a boy at the doctor's.
beats.ch15.s03.b008: She reads the room the way she reads a painting, one thing at a time. The travel clock says nine. The cuckoo says nine. Tea has dried brown on Roux's drawings. The wardrobe door stands ajar.
beats.ch15.s03.b010: She picks up his phone. The photographs from the tower are gone, every one, and the phone's clock says 09:00.
beats.ch15.s04.b001: She runs the whole way in the wrong boots. Clothilde said the young man in grey rented it.
beats.ch15.s04.b003: Tyre tracks show where the black four-by-four stood, already filling with fresh snow. Inside: a cold stove, a swept floor, a smell of candle wax. Nothing else.
beats.ch15.s05.b001: She brought him home on the Sunday night train, his head on her shoulder. Every hour he asked whether they were nearly at Saturday.
beats.ch15.s05.b003: The big easel is empty. A docket on the bench says the Fondation's courier took the Allegory on Friday, while they were in the snow. Morel signed for it.
beats.ch15.s05.b004: Morel hasn't answered his phone since Sunday. The atelier is hers now, and the sofa, and the man on it.
beats.ch15.s05.b005: On her own phone she has the REMIT page and the list of tests, saved before it died in the tower.
beats.ch15.s05.b006: The Panthéon line she has only in her head. She read it over Dec's shoulder by his torch, the night the trap banged shut, and said it aloud: five kilometres.
beats.ch15.s05.b008: A restorer remembering a notebook she no longer has. Nobody will believe that, and she knows it.
beats.ch15.s05.b011: Inès reads the last line four times. She puts the phone face down on the bench and doesn't touch it again until morning.
beats.ch15.s06.b001: The skylight has gone a strange thin grey, like light through a dirty window. On the bench, her laptop shows the live broadcast from the Panthéon.
beats.ch15.s06.b006: It's lovely. When did they take it?
beats.ch15.s06.b007: While we were in the snow.
beats.ch15.s06.b008: Waiters move along the front row with little pewter cups. The minister drinks. The prefect drinks. A banker raises his cup to the camera.
beats.ch15.s06.b009: Mulled wine. In April. Your man's very fancy.
beats.ch15.s06.b010: By a quarter to three the front row has gone soft. Heads tilt. A journalist smiles at nothing. Inès knows that smile. She has watched it on Dec for four days, and now she knows what was in the cups.
beats.ch15.s06.b011: Nobody on the broadcast seems to notice.
beats.ch15.s06.b012: Above them, the skylight dims to blue. The light drains from the room as if someone were drawing it off with a cloth.
beats.ch15.s06.b013: On the laptop the nave goes dark. Phones light up in it like fireflies.
beats.ch15.s06.b015: Down in the rue Vieille-du-Temple a car horn starts, then another, and they don't stop.
beats.ch15.s06.b016: On the screen a tall man stands at the lectern, silver hair swept back, perfectly calm. The camera loves him.
beats.ch15.s06.b017: Do not be afraid. The debt is called. For nine minutes, my friends, we will know what we owe.
beats.ch15.s06.b019: Behind him, in the dark, the pendulum swings past and back, and nobody stops anything.
beats.ch15.s06.b020: At three the light comes back, silver and slow. The clocks lurch and start. In the front row the minister lifts his head, tears on his face, and tells the camera he saw the hand of God.
beats.ch15.s06.b023: She looks at the skylight, and the laptop, and the man on the sofa who once told her a twenty-minute story about a cat called Pádraig to keep her alive.
beats.ch15.s06.b025: From her bench drawer she takes an old steel watch with a cracked strap. Zoltán's. She winds it, twelve slow turns, the way her father did at red lights. Then she takes off Dec's stopped watch and buckles her father's on in its place.
beats.ch15.s06.b026: It ticks. He holds it to his ear and smiles, as if she has given him the time.
beats.ch16.s01.b001: One lamp on the bench. Orange cloud sits in the skylight. Inès's notebook lies open under the lamp.
beats.ch16.s01.b003: Pichon's name glows on the screen. Dec's thumb hovers. He turns the phone face down on the cushion.
beats.ch16.s01.b006: She has what the tower left on her phone, and what the Jura left in her notebook.
beats.ch16.s01.b009: Nine ticks. Five letters in Vey's own hand. Four to go, and the last is an E or an L.
beats.ch16.s01.b010: She rings Les Bréviaires. Clothilde picks up on the second ring. A television mutters behind her.
beats.ch16.s01.b011: The honeymoon that isn't. Is he alive?
beats.ch16.s01.b012: Asleep on a sofa. Ma Mère, I need a word. Nine letters. REMIT, then three I can't read, and the last is an E.
beats.ch16.s01.b013: The sisters always said Vey repented at the end. A lender who repents does only one thing, child.
beats.ch16.s01.b014: Remittere. He lets the debt go. We say it at every absolution. In remissionem peccatorum.
beats.ch16.s01.b015: Inès writes it under the ticks. It fits, letter for letter, down to the flat foot of the E.
beats.ch16.s01.b017: Mutuo datum remittere hora nona. What was given as a loan, forgive at the ninth hour.
beats.ch16.s01.b018: And they scraped it off. Of course they did. Bankers.
beats.ch16.s01.b019: Inès. Drink nothing they pour you.
beats.ch16.s01.b020: She hangs up. Dec is sitting up, hair flat on one side.
beats.ch16.s01.b021: You did that with a phone call.
beats.ch16.s01.b022: Clothilde did it with a prayer. Don't make a thing of it.
beats.ch16.s01.b023: His phone buzzes against the cushion.
beats.ch16.s01.b025: He wants me inside. Grand. Galerie du dôme, the notebook said. That's the walk round the outside, on every tourist map.
beats.ch16.s01.b026: Fabien wiped the photograph. But Inès read that line over Dec's shoulder in the tower, by his torch, and said it out loud. She has said it to herself every night since.
beats.ch16.s01.b029: She opens the list of tests on her phone, all she kept of Morel's notebook.
beats.ch16.s01.b031: Every test reaches further. Jean-Paul checked the range. On long wave, range means a long wire, hung high.
beats.ch16.s01.b032: In Morel's drawer of gift-shop rubbish she finds a postcard of the Panthéon.
beats.ch16.s01.b034: Sixty-seven metres of steel, hanging free in the middle of Paris. It isn't only a pendulum, Dec. It's an aerial.
beats.ch16.s01.b035: Not the gallery outside. The one inside, at the top, where the cable hangs from.
beats.ch16.s01.b036: Then I swap the wine at half past two, the way Fabien said on the phone. And then I go up with the word.
beats.ch16.s02.b001: The cell in the crypt is finished, and with the pass nobody stops him.
beats.ch16.s02.b003: Kessler fills the arch of the roped south stair. The narrow north stair inside the wall has a new chain and a shiny brass padlock.
beats.ch16.s02.b004: Two minutes, that. Later, when nobody's looking.
beats.ch16.s03.b002: The CECI N'EST PAS UNE BOMBE crate goes over with theatrical surprise. Four hundred gears ring across the stone like all the coins in the world.
beats.ch16.s03.b003: Behind the screen, four pewter jugs of the real wine go into the empty crate. Four jugs of vin chaud with a spoon of cocoa take their place.
beats.ch16.s03.b004: Eleven euros forty an hour. For this, I want twelve.
beats.ch16.s03.b005: At half past two the trays go out. The minister drinks. The prefect drinks. The cardinal's secretary asks for a second cup.
beats.ch16.s03.b006: Dec watches them drink harmless wine and breathes out. Then he walks to the north aisle, not hurrying.
beats.ch16.s04.b001: Vaulmont's voice fills the nave behind him. Everyone is facing the stage.
beats.ch16.s04.b002: ...and when the light is taken from us, my friends, we will see what we truly owe...
beats.ch16.s04.b004: Seventy seconds. The shackle drops, and he goes up into the dark two steps at a time, the word ready in his mouth.
beats.ch16.s04.b005: By the easel, Inès feels a hum in her back teeth. It comes down the steel cable from the dome, and the brass sphere carries it past her.
beats.ch16.s04.b007: Forty steps up, a torch hits him from below.
beats.ch16.s04.b009: Not police. The prefect's own protection detail, who answer to the man in the front row and not to any commissaire. They have just watched a contractor pick a lock twenty metres from a minister.
beats.ch16.s04.b010: There's a radio up there! On the cable! Two minutes, I only need two minutes!
beats.ch16.s04.b011: They don't need two minutes. They need four seconds, and one of them twists his wrist until the picks fall.
beats.ch16.s05.b001: They are marching him down the north aisle when the light goes. The dome turns deep blue, and outside thousands of people sigh at once.
beats.ch16.s05.b003: Phones light up all over the nave, every screen at 09:00. Through the great doors the traffic lights of the rue Soufflot flash red.
beats.ch16.s05.b004: And the guests see it, wide awake and sober, cups in their hands. They will remember every second, because Dec made sure of it.
beats.ch16.s05.b005: The minister stands up. The cardinal's secretary crosses himself.
beats.ch16.s05.b006: Do not be afraid. For nine minutes the city will hear its debt. Mutuo datum.
beats.ch16.s05.b008: It's a radio! It's a box in the dome! It's a radio!
beats.ch16.s05.b011: At three the light comes back, silver and slow. Vaulmont lifts one hand, and the station clock lurches round to three.
beats.ch16.s05.b012: And now, my friends, it is given back.
beats.ch16.s05.b013: The nave stands and applauds. Some of them are weeping. The camera's red light stays on.
beats.ch16.s06.b001: Two hundred clocks are ticking, every one of them right.
beats.ch16.s06.b003: LE MIRACLE DU PANTHÉON. Front page. With a photograph of a clock.
beats.ch16.s06.b004: The Bourse lost billions in nine minutes. And somebody, it says here, has made billions.
beats.ch16.s06.b005: Nom de Dieu de nom de Dieu. It's a radio. I told him I wouldn't build it.
beats.ch16.s06.b008: The prefecture let him go at six this morning. Monsieur de Vaulmont declined to press charges.
beats.ch16.s06.b009: A foreigner, overexcited by an eclipse. He told them he'd hate to spoil such a beautiful day.
beats.ch16.s07.b001: The easel is empty. Dec sits on the sofa, a bruise coming up on one wrist.
beats.ch16.s07.b002: A courier has left two envelopes: one cream, one with a bank's blue logo.
beats.ch16.s07.b005: Clipped to it is a cheque: the fee for the Clockmaker's Cell, exactly as Dec invoiced it, to the cent.
beats.ch16.s07.b006: He paid me. And he let me go.
beats.ch16.s07.b007: Of course he did. He keeps accounts.
beats.ch16.s07.b010: He's called in the atelier. My bench, my lamps, Jean-Paul's sofa. Nine days.
beats.ch16.s07.b012: Lent to the Panthéon, it says in the paper. By popular demand.
beats.ch16.s07.b013: On her bench, under the lamp, her notebook still lies open at one word in pencil. REMITTERE.
